entry.title: SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Org Integration with SAP Field Service and Asset Management
entry.content:
The goal of this Integration is to ensure that users in SAP FSA to have the right permissions for access to business objects based on the organizational levels they are assigned in SAP S/4HANA. Both Initial and Delta load are supported.

In the past we have supported only Legacy Org Integration to FSA and with this new Integration, we support Enterprise Service org Integration as well providing the flexibility to the customers to choose the right organizational model that is applicable for them.

There are two parts to this Integration:

  • Part-1: Integrate the SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Organizational model/hierarchy to SAP FSA. Any changes or deletions to organizational units will be synchronized again to SAP FSA.
  • Part-2: Assign these organizational levels to technical objects (master and transactional) to ensure that appropriate access is granted to the users in SAP FSA 

Part-1: Enterprise Service Org Integration from SAP S/4HANA to SAP FSA

How to enable Enterprise Org Model?

Path: SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Service -> Basic Functions -> Enterprise Organizational Management -> Enable Enterprise Organizational Model

           

Enterprise Org Definition – This is required for Enterprise Service Org integration and also assignment determination of Ent. Service Org to assign to Business objects

Path: SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Enterprise Structure -> Definition -> Service -> Define Enterprise Service Organization

  • Define the Enterprise Service orgs, Hierarchies, Plant, Storage location, Service Profiles, Planning Plant in below path.

           

Sales Area Assignment - This is required for determination of Enterprise service org for assignment to Business objects(Master and Transaction Data)

Path: SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Enterprise Structure -> Assignment -> Service -> Assign Standard Enterprise Service Organization to Sales Area

  • Define the Sales area w.r.t enterprise service org in below path 

           

Fiori App: Manage Teams and Responsibilities - SAP Fiori Apps Reference Library – Use this app to create service teams, assign service orgs and service employees to the teams. Business role: SAP_BR_BUSINESS_PROCESS_SPEC (Business Process Specialist)

How the Manage Teams and Responsibilities app looks like in SAP S/4HANA?

  • Create a service Team ‘0101_000’
  • Select Category as ‘Service’ as only that relevant for FSA Enterprise Service Org integration
  • Team Type is configurable.
  • In the Responsibility Definitions view, maintain the Enterprise Service Org
  • In the Team Owners and Team Members views, assign the relevant service employees, and as function for the team members choose Executing Service Employee:

          

Team Types under Team category - ‘Service’  can be configured in below path

Path: SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Cross-Application Components -> General Application Functions -> Responsibility Management -> Teams and Responsibilities -> Team Categories -> Define Team Types

       

Functions classification for Team Category - ‘Service’  can be configured in below Path:

Path: SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Cross-Application Components -> General Application Functions -> Responsibility Management -> Teams and Responsibilities -> Team Categories -> Classify Functions for Team Category

         

Pre-requisites to Integrate to SAP FSA:

  • The minimum SAP S/4HANA version must be 2025 FPS02
  • DRF, RFC, Oauth Profile Setup, Client id, Client secret generation.
  • IMG Configurations
  • Service Employees assigned under Responsibilities Definition should be available in FSA.

How the Enterprise Org Structure looks like when replicated to SAP FSA?

Service teams will be assigned under Enterprise Service Org’s and Service Employees assigned in Teams and responsibilities Fiori app will be displayed under User Assignments.   

        

Default Flow: User Assignments->Enterprise Service Team->Enterprise Service Org

Additional Flow (Configurable)

  • Default flow will remain as is, in addition below is supported.
  • User Assignment (Team Members, Team Owners) -> Enterprise Service Org

Note: For Assignment of Team Owners to Ent Srv Org – Maintain Team Type and Assign Team to ESrvOrg. - SRVTEAMOWN (Service Team Owner). For Assignment of Team Members – Maintain Team Type and corresponding Member Function in below Path

Path: SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Service -> Integration with Other SAP Solutions -> SAP Field Service and Asset Management -> Master Data Replication -> Enterprise Organization -> Configure Business Partner assignment to Enterprise Service Org          

     

Extensibility: To provide further flexibility on assignment of service employees to only Enterprise Service Org and skip Service Teams, Below BADI is provided.

Business Context: “CRMS4_FSM_EORG_SRVTEAM”

Enhancement Spot

BADI

Description

ES_CRMS4_FSM_EORG_INT

CRMS4_FSM_SKIP_SRVTEAM

Skip Service Team Replication to FSA

The Custom Logic Fiori app lets you implement, activate, and transport BAdIs entirely from the browser — making it upgrade-stable, cloud-ready, and accessible without broad developer authorizations. 

Configurations to Integrate Enterprise Service Org’s and related data to SAP FSA:

  • IMG Configurations.
  • RFC, OAuth, Client Id and Client Secret generation.
  • DRF Configurations.

IMG Configurations:

Path: SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Service -> Integration with Other SAP Solutions -> SAP Field Service Management -> Configure Integration

  • Enable Enterprise Org Repl should be true for FSA Integration
  • Only Single company is supported, Maintain X-Account-ID and X-Company-ID in below
  • Specify the RFC destination that is created to establish the connection to FSA.
  • Specify the EntOrgS4CompanyID as "00001" as this is supported only for single company

           

RFC, OAuth, Client Id and Client Secret generation:

T-code: SM59 – To create RFC Destination

  

Maintain Oauth Profile in Login & Security

  

T-code: /oSOAUTH2_CLIENT – Creation of Oauth Profile – Maintain Oauth 2.0 Client ID & Secret here

            

  

Oauth Client Id and Secret should be generated in FSA Admin portal and enable the respective companies.

  

DRF Configurations:

Tcode : DRFIMG

Navigate to Define Custom Settings for Data Replication  Define Technical Settings ->Define Technical Settings for Business Systems,   

         

Define Business systems, BO’s 

          

Define Replication Model 

          

Assign outbound Implementation for the replication model

         

Assign Target systems for Replication Model/Outbound Implementation

         

Enter the outbound Parameter – PACK_SIZE_BULK- ‘100’

       

Activate the Replication Model

        

How to Run Initial Load?

T-code: DRFOUT

DRF Filter Criteria:

Delta changes are triggered automatically once DRF Replication model is active, necessary configurations are done, no external trigger required.

T-code: DRFLOG - To check the DRF Logs. Example below

Part-2: Enterprise Org Assignment to Business Objects:

Assignment to below Master and Transaction data for below business objects is supported for FSA Integration

  • Business Partners with Customer Role
  • Employees
  • Products
  • Equipment’s
  • Service Order

Pre-requisites:

  • Enterprise Service Orgs/Service Teams should be available in FSA
  • Enterprise Org Definition and Sales Area Assignment should be done in IMG Config
  • CPI Configurations to enable enterprise org assignment.

Business Partners with Customer Role:

  • Using the sales area in BP Customer, the relevant Enterprise Service Orgs will be determined based on mapping in Sales Area Assignment and correspondingly Service Teams are determined and assigned in FSA.  

           

Employees:

  • In SAP S/4HANA, the employees are assigned to service teams using ‘Manage Teams and Responsibilities’ app. The unit to which this employee is assigned(via the position) will be assigned as organizational level of the Person in SAP FSM. 

Products:

  • When Sales area is assigned relevant Enterprise Service Orgs and Service Teams are determined and assigned
  • When Plant/Storage Loc. is assigned relevant Enterprise Service Orgs and Service Teams are determined and assigned
  • When both Plant/Storage Loc. and Sales area is assigned, Sales area takes precedence and relevant service orgs and teams are determined and assigned.

           

           

Equipment's:

  • When Sales area is assigned relevant Enterprise Service Orgs and Service Teams are determined and assigned
  • When Planning Plant is assigned relevant Enterprise Service Orgs and Service Teams are determined and assigned

           

  • When both Planning Plant and Sales area is assigned, Sales area takes precedence and relevant service orgs and teams are determined and assigned.

Service Order:

  • After setting up Enterprise Organizational Management, in the service order, Service org and Service Team will be assigned.

CPI Configurations to enable Enterprise Org Assignment to Business Objects:

  1. Business Partners, Products, Service Order Enterprise org assignment happens via IFLOW.
  2. Enter the connection details on Configure -> Receiver -> S4Hana_EntOrgLevel on above iflows                                 
  3. To enable enterprise org, set 'true' on Configure -> More -> 'Enable Enterprise Org Assignment' in below iflows. 
     

Conclusion:

The Enhanced Enterprise Service Organization Integration and assignment to Master and Transaction Data empowers organizations to implement sophisticated service organization assignment strategies that align perfectly with their unique business requirements. 

This feature is now available in SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS02 ready to transform how your organization manages service transactions and organizational assignments. 

References:

  • Integration with SAP Field Service and Asset Management | SAP Help Portal
  • Configure Data Replication Framework for Business Objects | SAP Help Portal
  • Field Mapping | SAP Help Portal

entry.title: Generative AI vs Agentic AI in SAP: Understanding the Difference
entry.content:
Overview:

When I started learning about Artificial Intelligence (AI), I kept thinking about one thing: How can AI actually help businesses in their day-to-day work, especially in systems like SAP?

We know SAP helps businesses manage different processes such as finance, procurement, sales, inventory and supply chain. But with AI becoming more common, I wanted to understand how it could make these processes easier, smarter and more efficient.

While exploring on this topic, I came across two termsinologies that caught my attention: Generative AI and Agentic AI.

To be honest, at first, I found them quite similar and I wasn’t sure what really made them different. So, I started exploring how each of them works and how they could be used in real SAP business scenarios.

In this blog, I’ll share what I’ve learned so far, explain the difference between Generative AI and Agentic AI in simple terms and walk through a few practical examples from the SAP world.

Let’s understand it step by step!

 

What Is Generative AI?

  1. Creates content: Generative AI uses our instructions to generate text, explanations, code, and other content.
  2. Helps with SAP tasks: It can explain SAP processes, draft functional specifications, help us understand ABAP code, and prepare test scenarios.
  3. Needs verification: AI can make mistakes, so we should check its answers against our SAP system and business requirements.

How Does Generative AI Work?

  1. Learns patterns: The AI model learns patterns from large amounts of training data.
  2. Responds to prompts: We provide an instruction, and the model generates a response based on its training and available context.
  3. Improves through follow-up prompts: We can ask for simpler explanations, examples, or summaries, but the results still need to be checked.

 

 Picture 1: Generative AI vs  Agentic AI

 

What Is Agentic AI? 

  1. Works toward a goal: Agentic AI can plan and coordinate multiple steps to solve a problem.
  2. Uses connected tools: In SAP, an AI agent could check invoice details, compare purchase orders and goods receipts, and identify discrepancies.
  3. Supports next steps: It can recommend actions or perform approved tasks, depending on its integrations and permissions.

How Does Agentic AI Work?

  1. Understand and plan: Identify the goal and decide which steps are needed.
  2. Act and verify: Use authorized tools to gather information, check results, and perform additional checks if necessary.
  3. Respond or take action: Present the findings, recommend a solution, or initiate an approved action.

In simple terms: Generative AI helps us create answers; Agentic AI helps us work toward outcomes.

 

Generative AI vs Agentic AI: What Is the Difference?

Let's compare both concepts using following SAP examples.

 Picture 2: Which AI approach fits in the Task

They are connected concepts, and an AI agent may use a generative model as one of its core capabilities.

Generative AI focuses on generating useful outputs, while Agentic AI focuses on coordinating actions toward a goal.

 

How Does This Relate to SAP Joule? 

1. Meet SAP Joule: Joule is SAP’s AI copilot that brings AI assistance into supported SAP applications and workflows.

2. Ask in simple language: Users can ask questions naturally instead of navigating complex screens for every task, depending on the available features.

3. Understand business context: Joule can help users find information and understand business processes using relevant enterprise context and authorized data.

4. Go beyond answers: Supported AI agent capabilities can coordinate multiple steps across business processes and applications, depending on integrations and permissions.

5. Know the difference: Generative AI creates content, AI agents work toward goals using tools and actions, and Joule provides AI capabilities within SAP’s enterprise ecosystem.

The key takeaway: In SAP, AI is not just about getting answers. It’s about making business processes easier to understand, support and execute.

 

What Should SAP Professionals Keep in Mind?

As AI becomes more relevant to enterprise applications, I believe SAP professionals should keep a few important points in mind.

Picture 3: Key AI Considerations

For SAP consultants, developers, and business analysts, these considerations are just as important as understanding the technology itself.

 

Generative AI vs  Agentic AI: Pros & Cons

Like any technology, AI has its own pros and cons. In SAP, it can save time, reduce repetitive work, and make it easier to understand business processes. But it can also give incorrect answers, raise data security concerns, and require extra effort to integrate with existing systems. So, while AI can make our work easier, we still need to use it carefully and apply our own judgment.

 

 Picture 4: Generative AI vs  Agentic AI: Pros & Cons

 

Final Thoughts

I believe the first step is not to ask whether Generative AI or Agentic AI is better. Instead, we should ask what business problem we want to solve, what data and tools are required, and how AI can help us achieve the desired outcome safely and effectively.

AI in SAP is not just about generating answers. It is about finding practical ways to connect intelligence with business processes, reduce repetitive work, and help people make better decisions.

And understanding the difference between Generative AI and Agentic AI is a useful starting point for exploring that opportunity.

entry.title: Aynı Yasal Duyuru, Aynı Değişim… Yoksa Değil mi?
entry.content:
The Question

Open the roadmap. It looks familiar.

Open the H1 2027 Türkiye Payroll roadmap and the first impression is familiar.

Five Legal Changes.
New rules.
New dates.
New payroll work.

The normal question is obvious:

What do we need to change to stay compliant?

For TR00, the established payroll schema, that often means checking what is already supported, updating statutory parameters or enhancing existing logic where required, and keeping the solution aligned with applicable legislation.

Ama…

with TR01, our newer payroll schema, there is another question worth asking.

Can we respond to the legal change without creating the next special case?

And sometimes there is an even more important question: Should we build something new at all?

That changes how I read this roadmap. Not as five identical development commitments, but as five opportunities to make a deliberate product decision.

.......

TR01 is not about redesigning everything every time a new law arrives.

Compliance matters. Her zaman. But the best product response is not always a new payroll function or a new configuration table.

Sometimes we reuse something proven. Sometimes we automate manual administration. Sometimes a statutory scenario helps shape a reusable framework. And sometimes, after listening to the market, we decide that an implementation is not a priority for the current roadmap.

Some enhancements also began with our implementation partners, independently of any particular legal announcement. The legal changes give us a way to test whether those ideas can serve more than one scenario.

Here is how those decisions appear across the five roadmap topics, ordered by their current request delivery targets.

.......

Five Legal Changes, Five Product Decisions

The laws differ. So do the solutions.

Nitelikli Hizmet Merkezi Gelir Vergisi ve Damga Vergisi İstisnası

First, Qualified Service Centers.

The legal change provides an Income Tax and Stamp Tax exemption on qualifying remuneration for eligible personnel, up to a statutory ceiling: three times the gross minimum wage for standard centers and five times for eligible special locations. The amount above the ceiling remains taxable. SGK contributions are not changed by this specific exemption.

For TR00, we have not identified a relevant customer population. Consequently, a TR00 implementation is not planned in the current delivery scope. The legal obligation itself does not disappear for employers to whom it applies.

For TR01, the more valuable direction is not another hard-coded exception for one type of employer.

Instead, we plan a Configurable Statutory Exemption Framework with two distinct approaches: one for exemptions applied to an eligible remuneration base, and another for exemptions on specific additional payments, allowances or benefits.

The design direction includes configurable wage-type eligibility, statutory percentages and ceilings, relevant employee or workplace conditions, and distinct SGK, Income Tax and Stamp Tax treatments. Existing net-to-gross processing should apply those results consistently rather than requiring a separate gross-up engine.

Qualified Service Center is the immediate legal scenario. The ambition is a framework that can support other statutory exemptions when their rules require it.

Yani… not every new exemption deserves its own permanent branch in payroll logic.

.......

Kıdem Tazminatı Tavanı ve Vergiden Müstesna Çocuk Yardımı Tutarları

Next, child allowance.

For the second half of 2026, the Income Tax exemption thresholds for employer-paid child allowances are TRY 787.76 per child up to and including 72 months, and TRY 393.88 for children older than 72 months. Income Tax and SGK exemptions follow different statutory rules.

For TR00, we can build on the existing child-allowance and SGK treatment. The planned work focuses on the age-band Income Tax exemption and on making the allowance easier to maintain: enter the amount per child and eligible child count, then let payroll calculate the total.

For TR01, we can reduce a different manual step.

Instead of requiring HR to enter child counts repeatedly through age-band wage types, the planned enhancement reads IT0021 Family Members, determines eligible children and their age bands, and uses a configurable source for the employer-paid rate.

We are not introducing a separate SGK-to-Income-Tax-base configuration as part of this item. The objective is to automate the data that payroll already needs while preserving the established statutory calculations.

Less duplicate maintenance. More consistent eligibility data.

.......

Uzaktan Çalışma Yönetmeliğinde Değişiklik Yapıldı

Then, remote work.

The September 2026 amendment strengthens contractual requirements for hybrid arrangements, including the distinction between on-site and remote working days and hours. Employers also need to report remote-working days correctly through the applicable e-declaration process.

Here, the lesson is that reuse can be better than reinnovation by invention.

For TR00, reporting of remote-working days is already supported through the existing wage-type classification and e-declaration process, documented in SAP Note 3063529. The immediate task is to validate the customer configuration and the quantity passed to reporting, not to redesign SGK or Income Tax calculations.

For TR01, the planned approach is to reuse that proven pattern: identify the relevant wage type through Evaluation Class 11, carry its remote-working-day quantity in payroll results, and report it using HTRCEDE0.

We are not planning a new generic statutory day-count engine for this legal change. The source and treatment of partial remote-day quantities still need to follow confirmed legal rules and the appropriate existing configuration.

Sometimes the most scalable design decision is simply to avoid building something twice.

.......

SGK Turizm Ücret Desteği Genelgesi Yayımlandı

Tourism Wage Support leads to a different decision.

This temporary measure covers the period from May to December 2026. It is an employer-side support (destek), not an employee SGK or Income Tax exemption. The statutory model uses eligible SGK premium days and a daily amount of TRY 116.67, subject to the applicable employer-premium cap; SGK handles the official offset.

After considering partner feedback and identified customer demand, implementation of Tourism Wage Support is not planned for either TR00 or TR01 in the current scope. That is a product prioritization decision, not a change to employers' legal obligations.

Instead, we are prioritizing a separate TR01 enhancement that partners expect to deliver more everyday value: Recurring Meal Allowance.

Today, maintaining eligible meal days can involve repetitive entries and manual work when a daily rate changes during the month.

The planned TR01 enhancement uses a recurring IT0014 entry, derives eligible days from planned working days and applicable non-working-day information, and prorates the payment when the rate changes. It reuses existing SGK and Income Tax exemption processing rather than inventing new statutory meal rules.

One initiative is deliberately not being built now. Another, independent improvement is moving forward.

That is also a roadmap decision worth explaining.

.......

2027 Asgari Ücret Tespit Komisyonu Kararı ve Gelir Vergisi Tarifesi

And finally, the annual cycle.

At the time of this draft, the official 2027 minimum-wage and Income Tax parameters have not yet been announced. Based on the usual cycle, SAP localization expects the relevant announcements toward the end of December 2026; actual values and effective dates remain subject to the authorities' publications.

For TR00, the established priority is straightforward: update the relevant statutory parameters when confirmed, including the applicable severance ceiling on its own publication and effective-date schedule.

For TR01, the annual update sits alongside a more substantial foundation initiative: bringing Severance/Indemnity calculations into the payroll schema.

The first planned phase covers core statutory severance and notice indemnity calculations, together with a separate monthly severance provision. For that provision, payroll evaluates accumulated service and the applicable full provision at month-end, then calculates the adjustment against the previous month's closing provision balance.

That provision is an accounting calculation, not an employee payment; the precise financial and IFRS/TFRS treatment remains subject to validation.

More advanced termination settlement, off-cycle payment scenarios and annual leave provisioning or payout are possible future extensions, not part of the initial delivery commitment.

The opportunity is to establish a sound payroll foundation now without pretending that every related settlement scenario must be delivered at once.

.......

Beyond Legal Changes — Improving the TR01 Foundation

But not every improvement needs a new law.

During our Türkiye Payroll partner roundtables, some of the most valuable feedback came from everyday implementation experience.

A deduction carried into the wrong payroll split after a company change. A configuration value that consultants must enter manually. An Excel export that removes leading zeros from statutory reporting fields.

Small details?

Perhaps. Until they affect payroll accuracy, require unnecessary workarounds, or interrupt statutory reporting.

That is why, alongside the five Legal Changes, we have also prioritized six TR01 corrections and usability improvements, targeting the end of November 2026.

They address three practical areas:

  • Payroll correctness: Improving carry-forward deduction handling, wage-type processing flexibility, and payroll schema execution.
  • Configuration usability: Making T7TR parameter maintenance easier through search help and IMG integration.
  • Reporting reliability: Preserving leading zeros in E-Declaration Excel exports to avoid invalid reporting files.

None of these requires a new statutory announcement.

They come directly from implementation partners working with TR01 and identifying where the solution can work better.

İşte bu.

Reinnovation is not only about introducing new capabilities. Sometimes it means fixing what gets in the way of using the capabilities we already have.

.......

The Pattern

Put these decisions together and a different pattern emerges.

An established process → reuse and validate it before designing a replacement.

Repeated manual maintenance → derive information from existing employee or working-time data where appropriate.

A recurring statutory scenario → build a configurable framework when it creates genuine reuse.

Limited customer demand → make a transparent decision about what not to prioritize.

Everyday implementation friction → correct the foundation, even without a new law.

Three streams reinforce one another: statutory compliance, reusable product enhancements, and continuous improvement.

They do not always require the same technical response or the same delivery timeline.

.......

The Design Principle

Each legal change invites a design decision — not necessarily new development.

TR01 is not simply TR00 rewritten. And it is not a redesign project hiding behind every legal change.

It is a habit of asking one extra question when change arrives:

What is the simplest sustainable response — reuse, automation, configuration, a focused correction, or a conscious decision to defer?

Not every legal change will produce a reusable capability. Not every partner request will become a committed delivery. And not every proposed improvement needs a new engine.

But every decision should be clear about the customer problem it solves.

.......

Haydi Konuşalım

The best product decisions begin with the right conversations.

If you are implementing TR01, planning a migration, or following the H1 2027 legal changes closely — we have a dedicated space for you.

The Türkiye HCM Localization workspace is where SAP, customers, and partners share implementation experience, ask questions, and shape what comes next.

We have just opened a thread for this roadmap discussion:

Türkiye HCM — H1 2027 Legal Changes: What's Coming & Your Input Matters →

Your edge cases, your implementation experience, your questions — hepsi önemli.

.......

Son Söz

Same legal announcement.

Same need to understand the statutory impact.

But not necessarily the same product change.

TR00 continues to build on its established payroll design. TR01 gives us room to reuse what works, automate what is repetitive, configure what genuinely varies, and improve the foundation based on implementation experience.

These are roadmap intentions and delivery targets, not guarantees that every design detail or planned release date is fixed. Further engineering analysis, statutory guidance and customer feedback may affect the scope.

If you want to follow the progress of the Legal Changes, you can subscribe in SAP Regulatory Change Manager (RCM) for updates.

And I will leave you with a question:

Where in your payroll could a special case become a reusable rule — or where could an existing solution simply be made easier to use?

İşte bu.

entry.title: SAP Dynamic Forms 2609 Now Available – What's New?
entry.content:
The 2609 release is headlined by a significant new governance capability: configurable approval workflows for both form instances and form definitions. Alongside this, the release deepens integration with S/4HANA maintenance Fiori apps and includes a set of additional platform enhancements.

Together, these updates help organizations strengthen control over their form processes, connect field data more directly with maintenance operations, and improve the everyday experience of building and managing forms. 

Now, let's take a closer look at what's new in SAP Dynamic Forms 2609.

Approval Workflows for Forms

The most significant capability introduced in 2609 is configurable approval workflows for SAP Dynamic Forms. This new feature adds optional approval gates at two critical moments in the form lifecycle:

  • Form Instance Completion: A completed form can be routed for approval before it is marked as Completed.
  • Form Definition Publishing: A form design can be routed for approval before it is published and made available for use.

Approvals are routed through SAP Build Process Automation (SBPA), supporting multi-step, multi-reviewer processes without any custom code. The feature is enabled per form and per tenant, is off by default, and can be selectively activated only where approval governance is needed. It also works both online and offline — the same approval gate applies to forms filled in SAP Service and Asset Manager.

Submitting a Form Instance for Approval

When approval is configured for a form, users see a Submit for Approval option instead of the standard Complete action. Once submitted, the form becomes read-only and displays a 'Pending Approval' status. The submitter can cancel the approval at any time before a decision is made, in order to continue editing.

Reviewers act on the submitted form directly in the My Inbox app. The outcome follows a clear decision flow:

  • If Approved → the form moves automatically to Completed status.
  • If Rejected → the form reopens for editing, with reviewer feedback provided to the submitter.

An Approval Decision screen shows multi-reviewer feedback including who reviewed the form, when, and any comments — giving submitters full visibility into the review outcome.

Submitting a Form Definition for Approval

Designers publishing a new or updated form definition can use the Publish with Approval option in Form Builder. The form definition locks (becomes read-only) while under review and is routed to configured approvers through SBPA.

  • If Approved → the definition publishes automatically.
  • If Rejected → the definition unlocks, allowing the designer to revise and resubmit.

Configuring Approval Workflows

Approval workflows are configured directly from the Administration app, without requiring any development work. Key configuration capabilities include:

  • Approval Settings: Configure approval requirements for 'Form Instance Completion' and 'Form Definition Publish,' scoped to all forms in an application or to a specific form.
  • One-Click Tenant Enablement: The Approval Workflows tab in the Administration app provisions the workflow environment automatically with a single click.
  • Workflow Design: Use the embedded SBPA Studio drag-and-drop editor to define who approves and in what sequence.
  • Approval Monitoring: Track both active and completed approvals from within the Administration app.

 

Integration with S/4HANA and ECC

The approval workflow feature also integrates with S/4HANA and ECC environments, ensuring that approval outcomes are visible across the broader maintenance ecosystem:

  • Approval and rejection feedback is visible directly in Web Dynpro Apps, giving users in the back-end system visibility into the status of form reviews.
  • Mobile push notifications are sent to SAP Service and Asset Manager users whenever a form is approved or rejected, keeping field teams informed without requiring them to actively check for updates.

Integration with S/4HANA Maintenance Fiori Apps

The 2609 release introduces out-of-the-box integration between SAP Dynamic Forms and standard maintenance Fiori apps in S/4HANA, eliminating the need for custom extensions. The following apps are supported:

  • F5104A – Perform Maintenance Jobs
  • F4604 – Manage Maintenance Notifications and Orders
  • F2071 – Find Maintenance Notification
  • F2175 – Find Maintenance Order

This integration is delivered as part of S/4HANA 2025 FPS02.

Additional Enhancements

The 2609 release also includes a set of platform improvements that extend the capabilities of Form Builder and improve usability for both form designers and integrators:

  • Native Camera Control for Barcode Scanning: Forms now support barcode scanning directly using the native device camera, simplifying data capture in field and warehouse scenarios.
  • Integration Resources Page: A new Integration Resources page provides guidance and reference materials for customers and partners building integrations with SAP Dynamic Forms.
  • Measurement Points Custom Control in Form Builder: Form Builder has been extended to support configuration of Measurement Points Custom Controls, broadening the platform's support for asset-related data capture scenarios.

     

  • Copy-and-Paste for Dropdown Choices: Copy-and-paste support is now available for dropdown choice editors in Form Builder, reducing the effort required to manage and maintain choice lists.

Summary

The 2609 release of SAP Dynamic Forms strengthens the platform's governance capabilities with the introduction of configurable approval workflows, while also deepening integration with S/4HANA maintenance processes and improving the form authoring and field data capture experience. Together, these enhancements help organizations manage their form lifecycle with greater control, connect field findings more directly to maintenance workflows, and give form designers and administrators more powerful tools to build and manage forms at scale.

SAP Dynamic Forms 

Learn More

To stay current with SAP Dynamic Forms, explore the following resources:

  • Software Release Note for SAP Dynamic Forms
  • SAP Help Documentation
  • SAP Dynamic Forms Community

entry.title: Salary analysis report for internal candidates
entry.content:
I have recently had interest in a recruiting report that supports salary analysis for internal candidates. There are many ways to approach a request like this. I recently built a report that allows recruiting or compensation teams to view current and proposed job information for an internal candidate. This blog describes how I leveraged the SuccessFactors Story Reports, using a handful of its built-in capabilities, to deliver this report.

This is not intended to be a step-by-step guide. The goal is to highlight interesting usage of the Story Reports to demonstrate what it can achieve. A solid foundational knowledge of Story Reports is required to apply these ideas in your own instance. For details on any feature referenced here, you can learn more About Story Reports here.

 

My version of this report starts with two key sections:

  1. Current vs. proposed comparison – a side-by-side view of an internal candidate’s current information and the target information for the position they are applying to.
  2. Salary projection and compa-ratio – lets the report user model a new salary and see the resulting compa-ratio.

With these two views, the recruiting team can confirm that the proposed salary is both competitive and a reasonable increase before an offer is made.

 

Story Overview

This is designed to be an on-demand, one-candidate-at-a-time analysis rather than a mass report. When the report opens, the user is prompted to enter a Requisition ID and a User ID so the report focuses on a single internal application. (You can substitute an Application ID here if you prefer.)

 

Once these selections are applied, the report displays the identified requisition and internal candidate:

 

 

Data Source (Query) Design

The underlying query is shown below. It starts from Job Requisition and then branches into two join paths:

  • Path 1 (candidate): Job Requisition → Application → the candidate’s current User, Job, and Compensation information. This path tells us everything about who the candidate is today.
  • Path 2 (position): Job Requisition → Position Number. This path tells us about the position they are applying to.

You can extend either path with additional tables and choose whichever fields make sense for your own report.

 

Two query filters are important to consider:

  • ANSAL Only – This restricts results to the Annual Salary pay component from the compensation table, so figures are not duplicated or mixed across other pay components. This may need to be adjusted based on your Compensation Information configuration and the pay components available in your own instance.
  • Req ID – This is key for the user-prompted filters. It relies on input parameters, which must be defined first (see screenshot below). An input parameter defines a value the report user is allowed to supply at runtime – in our case, the Requisition ID and User ID.

 

 

Once the input parameters exist, you reference them inside the Req ID query filter, as seen here:

 

These two steps in the data source allow the report designer to edit the prompts at the story level.

 

 

Story Design

The first section presents the current and proposed position information. I generally recommend two separate tables stacked on top of each other – one for “current” and one for “proposed.” The table type, layout, and fields are entirely up to you. The key is to label every field clearly in your data source/query so there is no ambiguity once you’re working at the story level.

The salary analysis (section two) is more involved and makes creative use of several components and calculations:

  • My report uses a few pre-set percentage increases. I started with a list of simple calculations that take the candidate’s current salary and multiply it by various pre-defined percentages (e.g., 1%, 2%, 3%). Add as many or as few as you like using the standard calculation editor.

 

  • User-entered percentage increase. The previous percentages are fixed values set by the report designer. To let the report user enter their own percentage, add a calculation input control. The value the user enters can then be referenced in another calculation, so the projected salary updates dynamically based on their input.

 

  • Manually entering the candidate’s current salary is also an option if no current salary exists in the system – for example, if you extend this analysis to external candidates. You can add another input control so the report user can manually enter a current salary. That value can then be referenced in your salary calculations, wrapped in an IF/ELSE statement: the calculation uses the system salary when it exists and falls back to the manually entered salary when it doesn’t.

 

  • You can build similar calculations for compa-ratio, as seen below. Range penetration is a more complex calculation and isn’t part of my current design, although it is theoretically possible.

 

 

Additional Story Design

You can also add a third section that compares the projected salary to that of the candidate’s prospective new team. This requires at least one new data source/query. My example does not dynamically detect the candidate’s new team, although further automation is theoretically possible (though not something I have explored).

 

 

The query that drives this section is deliberately simple: it returns current job information for the entire organization. The tables and charts in this third section should be designed to surface the average salary and/or compa-ratio as needed. Using an input control, the report user selects one or several job codes, and the resulting metrics can be visually compared against the projected salary from section two. This helps the report user confirm the projected salary is in line with the rest of the new team.

You can create additional input controls to compare against other attributes – business unit, pay grade, and so on. If you want to compare two or more selections to the projected salary at once, create a separate data source for each so that each input control drives its own query.

 

That’s as far as I have taken this concept – feel free to experiment and share your own ideas below.

For specific questions or individualized help, reach out to your account team and ask for SuccessFactors Reporting Services.

 

Happy reporting, everyone!

entry.title: Re: Part 2 : SAP Datasphere: High-Level Overview
entry.content:
Hello @dohaidang_le 

SAP Datasphere allows you to make views from a Disk and In-Memory Space available in a Data Lake Space. This is useful when data modeled in SAP HANA Database storage needs to be consumed or processed within an SAP HANA Data Lake Files space.

Before You Start

Confirm that:

  • You have the appropriate SAP Datasphere privileges.
  • The target Data Lake Space has already been created.
  • The necessary Data Lake resources have been allocated.
  • The tenant meets the 128 GB minimum memory requirement.
  • The appropriate space has been designated for embedded SAP HANA data lake access.

Sharing the Views

Step 1: Open the source space
Go to Space Management, find the required Disk and In-Memory Space, and select Edit.

Step 2: Select the views
Identify the views you want to expose to the Data Lake Space.

Step 3: Configure sharing
Use cross-space sharing to make those views available outside the source space.

Step 4: Choose the target space
Select the appropriate Data Lake Space as the target.

Step 5: Deploy
Save and deploy the configuration. The shared views can then be accessed by authorized users in the Data Lake Space.

Important limitation: Data products cannot be published directly from a Disk and In-Memory Space in this scenario. Share the required views instead.

By Sonja Liénard, SVP, CPO of ABAP Platform, SAP SE

At SAP TechEd 2026, we are announcing innovations that take ABAP development further into the era of Agentic AI, building on everything we started at SAP TechEd 2025 and SAP Sapphire 2026. All these announcements point in the same direction: helping developers unlock intelligent automation, boost productivity, and build smarter enterprise solutions, regardless of where they are in their SAP journey.

Key highlights:

  • Three Agents on SAP Business AI Platform
  • SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment is now available on Alibaba Cloud
  • Major enhancements in the ABAP development tools 

Advancing the New Era of Agentic AI for ABAP Development

1. Agentic ABAP Development: Three AI Agents on SAP Business AI Platform

At SAP Sapphire 2026, we introduced our Custom Code Agents for SAP S/4HANA Migration. At SAP TechEd 2026, we are taking it further with three Agents on SAP Business AI Platform:

  • ABAP Custom Code Migration Agent
  • ABAP Clean Core Adaptation Agent
  • ABAP Application Modernization Agent

Custom Code Assistant (focus on ABAP)

These three AI agents are part of the Custom Code Assistant and work together to support the migration, adaptation, and modernization of ABAP custom code. The ABAP Custom Code Migration Agent helps accelerate custom code migration from SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA. It can execute SAP S/4HANA readiness checks, apply deterministic quick fixes, use AI-based fixes with high confidence scores, and track all changes in transport requests. The ABAP Clean Core Adaptation Agent will help identify, and address ABAP Test Cockpit findings related to clean core compliance, while the ABAP Application Modernization Agent will support the modernization of legacy ABAP code toward ABAP Cloud development. Visit this document for more information about Agentic ABAP development.

For customers who are still on ECC and getting ready for migration, there is also a practical update to the Custom Code Migration App. You can now download ABAP Test Cockpit quick fix instructions and transfer them to your ECC system and apply automated SAP S/4HANA code adjustments before the technical conversion starts.

2. SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment: Expanding Global Reach

You may have noticed the new product name: SAP BTP ABAP environment is now SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment. Read more about the name change in this blog post.

SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment is now available on Alibaba Cloud, marking another milestone in its multi-hyperscaler strategy. China (Shanghai) is the first supported region on Alibaba Cloud, which becomes the fifth supported infrastructure provider alongside SAP Cloud Infrastructure, AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. For details about availability and supported service plans, read the dedicated Alibaba Cloud announcement blog post.

We are also planning an offering for SAP Sovereign Cloud for SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment, currently targeted for Q2 2027.

3. Latest Updates in ABAP development tools

At SAP TechEd 2026, we continue to make ABAP development more open, AI-enabled, and compatible with the tools developers already use every day. The latest updates to ABAP development tools for Eclipse and ABAP development tools for Visual Studio Code bring significant advances for agentic development.

The official ABAP development tools MCP server received a major update, adding enhanced support for repository search, code editing, testing, transport handling, and integration with AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. For a detailed overview of the new capabilities and supported tools, read the dedicated blog post.

ABAP development tools for Visual Studio Code version 1.2 adds support for 23 additional object types and introduces the first ABAP-specific views, including Transport Organizer, ABAP Feeds, Version History, SQL Notebooks, and HANA Source Code Search, further enhancing AI-enabled ABAP development in Visual Studio Code. Read the release blog post to explore all new features and improvements.

ABAP AI and ABAP IDE strategy join forces

 

What This Means for ABAP Developers

These announcements highlight SAP's continued investment in AI-assisted and agentic ABAP development. The AI agents support the migration, clean-core adaptation, and modernization of custom code for SAP S/4HANA. The availability of SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment on Alibaba Cloud marks another milestone in its multi-hyperscaler availability. The latest updates to the ABAP development tools MCP server and ABAP development tools for Visual Studio Code bring new capabilities that help developers take advantage of AI-powered tools and modern development environments.

These innovations give ABAP developers more choice, more flexibility, and new ways to work with AI across the SAP development landscape. With AI handling more of the repetitive and time-consuming work, ABAP developers can focus on what creates real value: understanding the business, making good architectural decisions, and delivering solutions that last.

Sonja Liénard is Head of ABAP Platform at SAP SE. She leads the unit responsible for ABAP platform, ABAP Cloud, ABAP AI, and ABAP IDE strategy.

1. Is this SAP Cloud ALM tenant included under our current SAP support/subscription contract without additional licensing or subscription costs?

Yes. SAP Cloud ALM is included at no additional license or subscription fee for customers with SAP Enterprise Support or cloud subscriptions containing Enterprise Support, cloud editions.

See Usage Rights -> SAP Cloud ALM Usage Rights Scope

 

2. Will clicking "Start Provisioning" generate any additional charges?

No. The provisioning action itself does not trigger any charges

See Usage Rights -> SAP Cloud ALM Usage Rights Scope

The SAP Cloud ALM entitlement will only expire if ALL Cloud subscriptions expire for the Customer. If even a single Cloud subscription is still valid, it maintains the entitlement to SAP Cloud ALM.

Yes. SAP Cloud ALM explicitly supports SAP S/4HANA across all deployment types, including On-Premise.

 

5. Considering that we currently do not have SAP Solution Manager, does SAP recommend adopting SAP Cloud ALM directly for this scenario instead of implementing a new SAP Solution Manager environment?

Yes, and your situation is in fact the ideal scenario for a direct adoption of SAP Cloud ALM.

 

6. If we transition to RISE with SAP in the future, can the same SAP Cloud ALM tenant, project information and ALM approach continue to be used during and after the transition?

entry.title: ABAP Development Tools for VS Code 1.2: What Caught My Attention
entry.content:
SAP recently released ABAP Development Tools (ADT) for Visual Studio Code version 1.2, bringing several improvements to the ABAP development experience.

What caught my attention wasn't just the addition of new features. It was the direction SAP is taking: bringing more everyday ABAP development tasks into VS Code while making it easier to connect AI tools to the development environment.

Here are the changes I found most interesting.

Less Switching Between Tools

A developer's work rarely involves writing code alone. You also need to inspect transport requests, investigate errors, check object history, and validate data.

Version 1.2 introduces several new ABAP-specific views to help with these tasks:

  • Transport Organizer – Work with transport requests directly in VS Code.

  • SQL Notebooks – Explore data using ABAP SQL queries and preview the results.

  • Object Version History – Review previous versions of an object and compare changes.

  • ABAP Feeds Reader – Access information such as short dumps, Gateway error logs, and system messages.

These features may seem small individually, but they can make the development workflow more convenient by reducing the need to switch between tools.

More ABAP Objects, Fewer Limitations

Another useful improvement is support for 23 additional ABAP object types.

The additions cover areas such as CDS development, Data Dictionary objects, application jobs, transactions, packages, and Fiori-related objects.

For developers working across different parts of an SAP system, broader object support makes VS Code a more practical environment for everyday development.

The Bigger Change: ABAP MCP Server

The most interesting update, in my view, is the major revision of the ABAP MCP Server.

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It provides a standardized way for AI applications to interact with tools and systems.

With the updated server, compatible AI coding agents can access ABAP development capabilities through MCP, depending on the setup and configuration. SAP mentions tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Codex, and OpenCode.

This is worth watching because it moves beyond AI simply suggesting code. It creates a way for AI agents to interact with the development environment and assist with development workflows.

However, access must be configured deliberately. The server is disabled by default, and editing capabilities are not enabled by default. Appropriate permissions, testing, and developer review remain essential.

A Simpler Way to Configure Connections

Version 1.2 also introduces a dedicated New Destination… option for configuring system connections, making the setup process more convenient.

It's a smaller change, but improvements like this help make development tools easier to work with.

My Takeaway

ADT for VS Code 1.2 is more than a collection of new views and supported objects. The combination of a broader development environment and an updated MCP Server points toward a workflow where developers can use traditional tools and AI assistance side by side.

The important question now is how effectively these capabilities fit into real SAP development work—and how developers balance that convenience with proper validation and control.

Which part interests you most: the new development features or the possibilities opened up by the ABAP MCP Server?

entry.title: Manage Flexible Constraints for SAP Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling (SAP PP/DS)
entry.content:
Manage Flexible Constraints for SAP PP/DS

Plan Transparently. Control Production Consumption. Adapt to Change.

Introduction

Effective production planning requires more than balancing supply and demand. Planners also need transparency, control over production and procurement quantities, and the flexibility to adapt plans to changing business requirements.

Previously planners did not have complete visibility of all the key information such as KPIs, alerts etc. across different phases of planning such as tactical planning (SAP Integrated Business Planning) and operational planning (Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling for SAP S/4HANA). ​Without a consistent way to communicate planning limits and targets, decisions made in one system may be overwritten or not fully respected in another.

Flexible Constraints in SAP PP/DS address this challenge by allowing planners to define supply-related targets and limits that are considered during production planning.

Introduced with SAP S/4HANA OP2023 FPS2, this functionality has been further enhanced and optimized in subsequent releases, including OP2025 FPS2. These enhancements provide additional capabilities for managing constraints, handling large volumes of data, and controlling how constraints influence planning decisions.

In this post, we will explore the main concepts behind Flexible Constraints, their configuration and management in the Fiori application, and the key enhancements introduced in SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1.

​1. What Are Flexible Constraints?

Flexible Constraints are supply-related limits and targets considered during planning in SAP PP/DS. They help planners control how much supply should be planned for a specific product and location or for a particular source of supply.

Flexible Constraints support two main planning scenarios:

  • Integration with an external planning system: Flexible Constraints defined in an external planning system can be integrated into PP/DS using an OData service or a remote-enabled function module.
  • Local maintenance in SAP S/4HANA: Flexible Constraints can also be created and maintained directly in SAP S/4HANA PP/DS.

This approach helps ensure that prebuild and post-build decisions made by planners are reflected in operational planning and remain consistent across planning systems.

2. Main Types and Principles

Flexible Constraints define the desired or permitted supply quantities for a given planning period. Three types of quantity semantics are available:

  • Target Supply (soft constraint): Defines the desired supply quantity.
  • Minimum Supply (hard constraint): Defines the minimum supply quantity to be considered during planning.
  • Maximum Supply (hard constraint): Defines the maximum supply quantity to be considered during planning.

These values help planners communicate their supply expectations while distinguishing between preferred quantities and mandatory planning limits.

2.1. Recurrence and Time Buckets

Flexible Constraints can be maintained for different recurring time intervals:

  • Daily
  • Weekly
  • Monthly
  • Quarterly
  • Yearly
  • Custom, for example, biweekly

The selected recurrence determines the time buckets for which the constraints apply.

2.2. Granularity Levels

Granularity determines how specifically a Flexible Constraint applies. SAP PP/DS supports two main levels:

LOCPRD — Location Product

The constraint applies to a product at a specific location, independently of the individual source of supply.

LOCPRDSOS — Location Product Source of Supply

The constraint applies to a specific product, location, and source of supply.

LOCPRDSOS can be further divided into internal and external sources of supply.

LOCPRDSOS Internal

An internal source of supply represents in-house production based on the Production Data Structure (PDS). The relevant production source is determined using the material's MRP 3 settings, including the production version.

LOCPRDSOS External

An external source of supply represents external procurement and is based on the material's procurement settings and the relevant source of supply.

The supported external source-of-supply categories include:

  • Info Record
  • Scheduling Agreement
  • Subcontracting
  • Stock Transfer

The choice between LOCPRD and LOCPRDSOS depends on the level of control required. LOCPRD provides an overall supply target or limit for a product at a location, whereas LOCPRDSOS enables more detailed control over individual supply sources.

2.3. Planning Versions

Flexible Constraints can be used with either the active planning version (000) or an inactive planning version.

Using the active planning version supports operational planning, while an inactive planning version allows planners to simulate alternative scenarios and evaluate their impact without directly changing the active plan.

3. How Are Flexible Constraints Used in Planning?

Flexible Constraints are consumed during production planning through the SAP_PP_FLXC heuristic, which is built on top of the Standard Lots Heuristic.

The heuristic considers the relevant Flexible Constraints during its planning run, helping align planned supply with the defined minimum, target, and maximum quantities.

From SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1 onward, priority and penalty settings provide additional ways to influence how Flexible Constraints are considered during planning.

4. Manage Flexible Constraints for PP/DS — Fiori App F7726

The SAP Fiori application F7726 — Manage Flexible Constraints for PP/DS provides a central interface for creating, updating, copying, deleting, and processing Flexible Constraints.

Let's look at the main functions available in the application.

4.1. Creation

Flexible Constraints Group IDs are created from the list page of the Manage Flexible Constraints for PP/DS application by selecting Create.

All mandatory fields must be completed before the constraint group can be created

The application validates overlapping periods. Flexible Constraints cannot be created for the same location-product scope for an overlapping time period. If an overlap is detected, a validation error is displayed, and the new FLXC Group ID is not created.

4.2. Update

Existing Flexible Constraints can be edited, provided the following value relationship is maintained:

Minimum FLXC ≤ Target FLXC ≤ Maximum FLXC

Two different meanings can be represented by a value of zero:

  • Zero with a unit of measure (UoM): The constraint is explicitly maintained with a value of zero.
  • Zero without a UoM: The constraint value is not maintained.

This distinction is important when interpreting and updating constraint data.

The active or inactive status is maintained at the individual bucket level. Active buckets participate in planning, while inactive buckets are excluded. If necessary, a bucket can be deactivated in Edit mode.

4.3. Copy

The application provides three options for copying Flexible Constraints from the list page. These options allow planners to reuse existing planning logic while adapting the constraints to different products or locations.

Copy from Template

The constraint is copied on a one-to-one basis to another target product location. During copying, the planning version, priority, and period can be changed.

Absolute values

Minimum, Target, and Maximum values can be entered directly for the target product location.

Relative to Template

Minimum, Target, and Maximum values for the target product location can be maintained as percentages of the corresponding values from the source product location.

4.4. Deletion

Deletion functionality for Flexible Constraints was introduced with SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1.

The application provides several deletion options, depending on the object and the data to be removed.

Delete from the List Page

Past and inactive FLXC Group IDs can be deleted from the list page using the Delete button.

Delete from the Object Page

An inactive FLXC Group ID can be deleted from its object page using the Delete button.

Delete All Inactive and Past Constraints

Within an FLXC Group ID, inactive or past buckets can be removed using the dedicated Delete All Inactive and Past Constraints button on the object page.

These options help maintain clean and manageable Flexible Constraints data.

5. Managing Large Volumes of Flexible Constraints

When Flexible Constraints need to be maintained for many products, locations, or sources of supply, manual processing can become inefficient.

The Manage Flexible Constraints for PP/DS application provides Excel-based functions to simplify mass creation, download, and update activities.

5.1. Get Template

Select Get Template on the list page to download the Excel template.

The workbook includes an additional page with instructions for preparing Flexible Constraints data.

5.2. Create from Excel

After entering the required data into the Excel template, upload the file using Create from Excel.

Both LOCPRD and LOCPRDSOS records can be created through this function. For large volumes of data, processing takes place in the background, resulting in the creation of new FLXC Group IDs.

If the uploaded file contains incorrect data or overlaps with existing records, the system displays validation errors to indicate where corrections are required.

5.3. Download in Excel

To export existing Flexible Constraints, select the required Group IDs on the list page and choose Download in Excel. The resulting workbook is downloaded to the local computer.

Starting with SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1, the download functionality provides two enhanced Excel files containing the main Flexible Constraints parameters, together with an additional Excel file containing priority and penalty attributes.

5.4. Update from Excel

Existing Flexible Constraints data can be updated in the downloaded Excel files, subject to the applicable Flexible Constraints logic and validations.

After making the required changes, upload the relevant file using Update from Excel.

These Excel-based capabilities make it easier to manage large datasets while retaining system validation of the uploaded information.

6. Priority — An Enhancement Introduced in OP2025 FPS1

Starting with SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1, each Flexible Constraints Group ID includes a Priority section.

Priorities range from A to O:

  • A: Highest priority
  • O: Lowest priority

A newly created FLXC Group ID is assigned priority A by default.

Priority can be maintained when creating an FLXC Group ID or updated later using the Edit function.

How Does Priority Influence Planning?

Priority settings are used by the SAP_PP_FLXC heuristic during planning.

By default, the heuristic considers the highest priority, A. However, planners can select another priority from the available list.

During a heuristic run, the selected priority and all higher priorities are considered by the Flexible Constraints planning logic. Constraints outside the considered priority range are ignored by the heuristic.

This functionality provides additional control over which Flexible Constraints influence a particular planning run.

7. Penalty — An Enhancement Introduced in OP2025 FPS1

Another enhancement introduced with SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1 is the Penalty section.

Penalty settings can be maintained when creating or updating Flexible Constraints. This section is optional and can be left blank.

The object page of an FLXC Group ID provides the following penalty types and indicators.

7.1. Available Penalty Types

Below Minimum Supply

  • Penalty value: Free-value input field
  • Minimum Supply Penalty Indicator: Active or Inactive

Deviating Target Supply

  • Penalty value: Free-value input field
  • Target Supply Penalty Indicator:
    • Active Below and Exceeding Target Supply
    • Active Below Target Supply
    • Active Exceeding Target Supply
    • Inactive

Above Maximum Supply

  • Penalty value: Free-value input field
  • Maximum Supply Penalty Indicator: Active or Inactive

These settings allow planners to maintain penalty-related parameters for deviations from the defined supply limits and target quantities.

Together with priorities, penalty attributes extend the options available for controlling how Flexible Constraints are used in planning.

8. Flexible Constraints Logic: Important Considerations

When working with Flexible Constraints, it is important to understand how overlap validation and the relationships between LOCPRD and LOCPRDSOS records are handled.

8.1. Overlap Validation

The system prevents the creation of overlapping Flexible Constraints for the same location-product scope (LOCPRD) during the same time period.

This validation helps avoid conflicting constraints for the same product and location.

8.2. Combining LOCPRD and LOCPRDSOS Constraints

LOCPRD and multiple LOCPRDSOS records can be created for the same product location and time bucket, provided the applicable value logic is respected.

The following rules are important:

  • Minimum Supply: The sum of the LOCPRDSOS minimum values can exceed the LOCPRD minimum value.
  • Target Supply: A validation error is displayed when the sum of all LOCPRDSOS target values exceeds the LOCPRD target value.
  • Maximum Supply: A validation error is displayed when the sum of all LOCPRDSOS maximum values exceeds the LOCPRD target value.

These rules should be considered when designing Flexible Constraints for scenarios involving multiple sources of supply.

Understanding the relationship between product-location constraints and source-of-supply constraints is essential for avoiding validation errors and maintaining consistent planning logic.

Conclusion

Flexible Constraints provide SAP PP/DS planners with a structured way to manage supply-related targets and limits across products, locations, sources of supply, and planning periods.

By supporting integration with external planning systems as well as local maintenance in SAP S/4HANA, they help improve transparency and consistency between tactical and operational planning. The Manage Flexible Constraints for PP/DS Fiori application further simplifies day-to-day maintenance through creation, editing, copying, deletion, and Excel-based mass processing.

The enhancements introduced in SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1, particularly priority and penalty settings, extend the possibilities for controlling how constraints influence planning decisions.

For organizations managing complex production and procurement scenarios, Flexible Constraints can be an important tool for translating planning targets into operational supply decisions while supporting simulation, prioritization, and more controlled production planning.

Have you already implemented Flexible Constraints in SAP PP/DS? I would be interested to hear about your experience, especially with priority settings, penalty parameters, and integration with SAP IBP.

If you found this post useful, I would really appreciate your support with a like. It encourages me to continue sharing practical SAP PP/DS insights and tips.

Enjoy your planning!

Since:

  • The same vendor and material are used
  • The same Tax Jurisdiction Code, Postal Code, and Address data are maintained

the remaining tax-relevant difference appears to be the Company Code (CC100 vs CC200).

I would recommend verifying the following:

1. Vertex Company Code Mapping

Please check whether both company codes are mapped identically in the Vertex integration configuration.

A common cause is that one company code is configured in Vertex as tax-exempt (or has a specific tax treatment), while the other company code is treated as taxable. Even if the SAP data is identical, Vertex can return different tax results based on the legal entity/company information sent in the request.

2. Compare the Actual Vertex Request Payload

Since Vertex determines the tax amount, the most valuable comparison would be the outbound request from SAP for:

  • Plant 100 / CC100 PO
  • Plant 200 / CC200 PO

Compare fields such as:

  • Company Code
  • Company Tax Registration
  • Legal Entity
  • Ship-To Location
  • Bill-To Location
  • Entity Use Code
  • Tax Area
  • Tax Jurisdiction

Even one different value can cause Vertex to return a different tax result.

3. Check Company Code Tax Configuration

Please verify whether there are any differences between CC100 and CC200 in:

  • Tax registration numbers
  • Tax-relevant company code settings
  • Vertex company assignments
  • RFC destination parameters or company-specific tax settings

4. Review Vertex Transaction Logs

Since the business expectation is that no tax should be calculated for this company code/plant combination, I would ask Vertex support to compare the transaction traces for both purchase orders and identify which field caused one transaction to be considered taxable.

  • EXIT_SAPLFYTX_USER_001
  • ZXFYTUxx includes
  • BAdIs or custom tax determination logic
  • User exits in MM purchasing processing

Most Likely Root Cause

Given that all plant address and jurisdiction data are identical and NAVS determination is successful, I would now suspect a Vertex company code/legal entity configuration difference between CC100 and CC200 rather than a standard SAP MM tax determination issue.

entry.title: Putting the SAP Cloud ALM Service Request API with AI help to Work
entry.content:
If you run SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, service requests are part of your daily routine. Examples include system refreshes, maintenance activities and technical changes in the landscape. For a long time, keeping track of them meant logging in to SAP for Me and clicking through lists.

When I learned that SAP Cloud ALM offers a Service Request API, I immediately wanted to use it for automation.

In this post I share how we went from a simple calendar integration to an AI agent in Microsoft Copilot Studio. The agent answers questions about our service requests, our SAP landscape and our SAP support cases. I also describe the architecture behind it and why I think this pattern is worth a look for every Private Cloud customer.

The Service Request API in a nutshell

The SAP Cloud ALM Service Request API extends the SAP Cloud ALM ITSM API. It gives programmatic access to service requests in the SAP Support Backbone, no matter whether they were created in SAP for Me, in SAP Solution Manager or through another support channel.

According to the documentation, it offers:

  • Omnichannel visibility: all service requests for your installation numbers.
  • Lifecycle monitoring: status, open/closed state and the "Party in Charge" (SAP or customer).
  • Activity and audit history: status changes, scheduling updates and modifications.
  • Communication: comments exchanged between your organization and SAP.

The API is built around these resources: service requests, service request items, activities, comments, parameters and contacts.

Step 1: Service requests in our Outlook calendar

The first building block was an integration flow in SAP Integration Suite. It:

  1. reads the service requests from the Service Request API,
  2. converts them into the iCalendar format (ICS), and
  3. exposes the result as an ICS file that can be retrieved online.

In Outlook, we subscribe to this file as an internet calendar. Every scheduled service request now appears as a calendar entry, visible to the whole team next to all our other appointments.

Yes, I know, SAP for Me has its own calendar. But we like to have everything in one central place.

Step 2: Why we wanted a real agent

The calendar answers the question when. Our daily questions are usually what, why, which system and who is waiting for whom. So we decided to build an agent instead of a dashboard.

These were our reasons:

  1. The information is spread across many places. Service requests, support cases, landscape data and our internal system list each live in their own tool, with their own UI and their own search. Finding the right place is often more work than reading the answer, and SAP for me is always a challange. 
  2. Questions instead of filters. Asking "Which service requests are waiting for us?" is faster than building a filter in a list view.
  3. Choosing the right service request is not trivial. The service request catalog for SAP Private Cloud is large. Picking the right template takes experience, and the agent can bring that knowledge to every team member.
  4. Live data and team knowledge in one answer. The agent combines live API data with our own documentation and system list.
  5. It works where the team already works. The agent runs in Microsoft Teams, on desktop and mobile. There is no new portal and no extra login.
  6. Easier onboarding and less dependency on individual knowledge. New colleagues get answers without having to know which portal holds which information.
  7. A safe starting point. The Service Request API is read-only, so the agent cannot accidentally change anything there.
  8. We could build it with what we already have. Copilot Studio was already available in our company, and SAP BTP was already in place. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard, so the server can be reused by other MCP clients as well.

Architecture

User and clients. Users talk to the agent in Microsoft Teams, on desktop or mobile.

Microsoft Copilot Studio. The agent ("SR Agent") lives here. Its instructions define its role, tone and rules. Copilot Studio's generative orchestration decides when to answer from knowledge and when to call a tool. The agent has two kinds of knowledge:

  • Static information: a curated knowledge base about SAP Private Cloud and the service request catalog, for example "Which service request do I need for …?"
  • System list: our internal system list on SharePoint.

MCP server on SAP BTP. The live data comes from our own MCP server. It runs as an application in a Cloud Foundry space of our BTP subaccount. Copilot Studio connects to it natively via MCP. The server exposes a small set of well-described tools, such as listing upcoming service requests, reading a service request, listing systems and reading support cases.

SAP Cloud ALM APIs. The MCP server calls the SAP Cloud ALM REST APIs:

  • Service Request API for service requests
  • Landscape API for landscape information: systems, cloud services and business services, with properties such as role, system number and data center
  • ITSM API for SAP support cases

SAP Central Support Services. SAP Cloud ALM is connected to the SAP Support Backbone, which includes SAP for Me, SAP Enterprise Cloud Services, the support service systems and ITSM. Whatever is created in SAP for Me is therefore also visible to the agent.

 

What the agent can do today

  • Service requests: upcoming and open requests, status, items, parameters, activity history and comments, and who is currently in charge.
  • Landscape: systems and their properties from SAP Cloud ALM, such as role, system number and data center, combined with our internal system list.
  • Support cases: we have already extended the agent to the ITSM API, so it can also access our SAP support cases.
  • Know-how: the right service request for a task, plus general information about SAP Private Cloud.

 

Example questions

Here are some questions our team asks the agent:

Service requests

  • "Which service requests are scheduled for next week?"
  • "Are there any open service requests where SAP is waiting for our input?"
  • "Summarize the status and the latest comments of service request 1234567."
  • "What has changed on our service requests since Monday?"

Choosing the right service request

  • "Which service request do I need for a system copy from production to quality assurance?"
  • "What information do I need to prepare before I open this service request?"

Landscape

  • "Which systems belong to our S/4HANA landscape?"
  • "What is the system number of our quality assurance system?"

Support cases

  • "Show me all open SAP support cases with high priority."

Combined

  • "Is anything planned for our production system this week, and are there open support cases for it?"

 

What's next

According to the documentation, creating and updating service requests through the Service Request API is planned for future releases. I really hope this comes soon, because filling in service requests manually is one of the least favourite tasks in our team. Honestly, there is hardly anything worse...

Useful links

  • Service Request API – SAP Help Portal
  • SAP Cloud ALM Service Request API – SAP Business Accelerator Hub
  • ITSM API – SAP Help Portal
  • SAP Cloud ALM ITSM API – SAP Business Accelerator Hub
  • Landscape API – SAP Help Portal
  • APIs in SAP Cloud ALM – overview
