entry.title: Agentic AI in SAP Development: The Real Challenge Is Not Writing Code
entry.content:
My experience working with AI-assisted SAP remediation changed how I look at AI in development.

Before working with these tools, it was easy to think of AI coding assistants mainly as tools that explain code, suggest corrections, or generate a few lines of ABAP. But when AI becomes part of an actual development workflow, the interesting part is no longer just the code it generates. It is how it helps move the entire task forward.

That is why the recent developments around SAP's ABAP MCP Server caught my attention.

The difficult part of SAP development isn't always the code

In SAP projects, changing a program is often only one part of the job.

You need to understand why the program exists, identify what needs to change, account for dependencies, validate the result, and make sure the business process still works as expected.

I saw this during my work on SAP remediation with KTern.AI CodeGenie. The work involved reviewing existing programs, understanding the required changes, and testing the updated logic.

One lesson stood out: getting code changed was not the same as getting the job completed.

Testing could be just as challenging. Sometimes, the initial test cases returned no data. We had to investigate the available master data, configuration, and selection criteria before finding a scenario that could properly validate the program.

AI assistance was useful, but the outcome still depended on understanding the SAP system and checking whether the results made sense.

That experience is one reason I find the move towards agentic AI interesting.

From generating code to participating in the workflow

SAP's updated ABAP MCP Server introduces a more flexible way for compatible AI clients to interact with ABAP development tools.

MCP, or Model Context Protocol, provides a standard way for AI applications to access tools exposed by another system. In this case, it helps connect compatible AI agents with supported ABAP development capabilities.

SAP's update mentions compatibility with tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Codex, and OpenCode, subject to the required configuration.

This is a meaningful development because it opens the door to workflows where an AI agent can do more than return a code suggestion in a chat window. It can use available tools to assist with development tasks.

For anyone interested in the technical changes behind this, I covered the release in my earlier article: ABAP Development Tools for VS Code 1.2: What Caught My Attention.

But how much should we trust the agent?

This is the question I find more interesting than how much code AI can generate.

A program can activate successfully and still produce the wrong business result. A report can execute without errors and return incomplete data. A technically valid correction can also miss the original business requirement.

These are not problems that disappear simply because an AI agent has access to more tools.

In SAP, the context matters. Understanding the business requirement, organizational structure, master data, configuration, and expected output remains essential.

An agent may help investigate a problem and carry out supported steps, but someone still needs to determine whether the proposed solution is correct. The same applies to authorizations, transport decisions, and testing.

SAP's MCP capabilities also depend on configuration and permissions; they should not be confused with unrestricted autonomous access to an SAP system.

For me, this is where the real value of agentic AI will be decided: not by how independently it operates, but by how reliably it works within a controlled development process.

What this means for SAP consultants

I don't think every SAP consultant needs to become an AI developer. But I do think we need to understand how these tools work and where they fit into our existing responsibilities.

Functional consultants bring business context. ABAP developers bring technical expertise. Both are needed to validate the outcome.

AI agents may reduce some repetitive work and help connect steps that developers previously performed manually. However, the ability to review results, identify incorrect assumptions, and test against real business requirements becomes even more important.

My takeaway: AI can help move SAP development forward, but moving faster only matters when we're moving in the right direction.

I'm interested to hear from others in the SAP community: Have you started using AI agents in your SAP development or support work? Where have you found them genuinely useful, and where do you still prefer to rely on manual investigation?

References

  • ABAP Development Tools MCP Server: Major Update Available!

  • ABAP Development Tools for VS Code 1.2: What's New and Why It Matters

Note: My remediation experience involved KTern.AI CodeGenie; it was not a project using the newly updated ABAP MCP Server. The two are distinct tools, and the experience above informs my perspective rather than serving as a direct evaluation of the MCP Server.

entry.title: RAP unmanaged BO: BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC dumps in saver – best approach?
entry.content:
Hello,

I'm building a Fiori Elements app (OData V4, RAP) that posts goods issue (PGI) for outbound deliveries, and I'd like advice on which approach is most appropriate.

Environment

  • SAP S/4HANA 2023 FPS03 on-premise (S4CORE 108 SP03), SAP_BASIS 7.58 SP03
  • Standard ABAP package (not ABAP Cloud)

Why I can't use a released RAP BO

  • I_OutboundDeliveryTP / R_OutboundDeliveryTP only offer CreateDlvFromSalesDocument and CreateDlvItemFromSalesDocument. There is no PGI action, header update is not enabled, and OverallGoodsMovementStatus / ActualGoodsMovementDate are read-only.
  • I_MaterialDocumentTP can create a material document, but it doesn't update the delivery status, document flow, or billing due index, so it doesn't replace delivery-based PGI.

So I use BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC with HEADER_CONTROL-POST_GI_FLG = 'X' in an unmanaged BO (read-only list of deliveries + one instance action postGoodsIssue, no own persistence, no draft).

Problem

My first version called the BAPI in the saver's save method. It works when PGI succeeds. When the BAPI hits a business error, it ends with BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT:

LSC_ZI_PGI_CR=>SAVE
  -> BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC  (SAPLV50I)
    -> FORM ROLLBACK_CHECK           (LV50IF01)
       >>>>> ROLLBACK WORK.

The BAPI executes ROLLBACK WORK itself on error, which is forbidden in the RAP save phase. The user only sees "ABAP Runtime error 'BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT'" and never the real error message.

Options I'm considering

A) sRFC in the action handler (current solution)

In the action handler (interaction phase) I call the BAPI with DESTINATION 'NONE', then BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT / BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK in the same RFC session, and then RFC_CONNECTION_CLOSE. The saver does nothing.

CALL FUNCTION 'BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC'
  DESTINATION 'NONE'
  EXPORTING header_data = ls_header header_control = ls_control delivery = iv_vbeln
  TABLES    return = lt_return
  EXCEPTIONS system_failure = 1 MESSAGE lv_msg communication_failure = 2 MESSAGE lv_msg OTHERS = 3.
" no error -> BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT DESTINATION 'NONE', else BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK DESTINATION 'NONE'
  • Pros: no dump. Standard messages (e.g. M7 021 stock deficit, delivery locked, missing CO account assignment) are returned to the UI immediately.
  • Cons: PGI is committed outside the RAP LUW, so a later ROLLBACK ENTITIES or a failure elsewhere in the same request cannot undo it. I also can't lock the delivery in the RAP lock method, because the RFC session is a different lock owner and the BAPI would collide with it.

B) BAPI in the saver, accept dumps on error

Keep the BAPI in save so PGI is part of the RAP LUW and RAP commits it. To reduce dumps I added pre-checks in the action handler: lock (ENQUEUE_EVVBLKE), picking/GI status, storage location, MM period (MARV), and unrestricted stock (MARD/MCHB).

  • Pros: transactionally consistent with RAP.
  • Cons: any error the pre-checks don't anticipate still dumps. In my test, a delivery passed all pre-checks but failed because of a missing CO account assignment (OKB9), and it dumped. The BAPI has no test/simulation mode I could call in check_before_save.

C) bgPF

Register the PGI in save with cl_bgmc_process_factory and run it after the RAP commit using an uncontrolled operation (IF_BGMC_OP_SINGLE_TX_UNCONTR), since the BAPI needs to roll back on its own.

  • Pros: runs only if the RAP transaction commits.
  • Cons: asynchronous, so the user doesn't get the result or error immediately, and I'd need extra logging/status handling. I also found a hint that RAP should use controlled operations (set_operation), but a controlled operation would dump on the BAPI's ROLLBACK WORK again.

Questions

  1. For a legacy BAPI that executes ROLLBACK WORK internally, which approach is recommended or supported in RAP: A, B, C, or something else?
  2. Is a synchronous RFC (DESTINATION 'NONE') in the interaction phase of an unmanaged BO considered acceptable, or is it expected to be restricted by runtime checks in later releases?
  3. Is registering an uncontrolled bgPF operation from the RAP save phase allowed?
  4. Is there a released API or a newer RAP BO for outbound delivery PGI that I missed?

Thank you in advance!

entry.title: SAP ABAP Purchase Order Release Audit Report with Document Flow Navigation
entry.content:
Introduction:
If you work with SAP, you know that Purchase Orders (POs), Purchase Requisitions (PRs), and Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) almost always require an approval process, known as a release strategy.
When audit season rolls around, the same questions always pop up:
Who approved this document? When exactly did they do it? What level of approval was it? And how does it tie back to the original PR, LTA, or Sales Order?
Here is the frustrating part: SAP updates the current status in tables like EKKO and EBAN, but it doesn't easily show the historical "who" and "when." Since there is no out-of-the-box standard report that tracks this entire chain (PO → PR → LTA → SO), auditors usually have to dig through documents manually, one by one.
To solve this, I’ll show you how to build a custom PO Release Audit Report in ABAP. This report captures the approver's user ID, full name, exact date, time, and approval level. Plus, it features a clean, single-screen ALV grid using CL_SALV_TABLE—allowing you to click and drill down into the details, and jump back with a single click, completely eliminating annoying pop-up windows.

Solution Review:
Solution at a Glance
The report reads the release status and its change history, finds the linked documents, and shows everything in one ALV where each click goes one level deeper.

Selection screen (PO / PR / LTA / SO)
        │
        ▼
   GET_DATA ──► starting documents (EKKO / EBAN / VBAK)
        │
        ▼
GET_RELEASE_HISTORY ──► CDHDR + CDPOS + USER_ADDR
        │
        ▼
   ALV display (CL_SALV_TABLE)
        │
   click Document No.          click Source
        │                          │
        ▼                          ▼
   DO_DRILL                    DO_BACK
 (GET_CHAIN → next level)   (restore previous list)

Design Decisions

Release data from change documents

EKKO and EBAN hold only the current release status (FRGZU). The user, date and time are in the change documents:
CDHDR has the username, date and time.
CDPOS has the new value of FRGZU.
USER_ADDR has the full name.
The report uses object class EINKBELEG for PO and LTA, and BANF for PR.


Same ALV, no popup
Instead of opening a new ALV each time, the report replaces the data and refreshes the same grid. Popups are avoided because they stack up and are harder to navigate.

Advantages
One report instead of checking ME23N, ME53N, VA03 and change documents one by one.
Shows release user, date, time and level together.
Follows the whole PO → PR → LTA → SO chain.
Simple navigation, with no popups.
The history-stack pattern is reusable in other ALV reports.


Step 1: Output structure

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_out,
         lvl       TYPE n LENGTH 1,        " PO=1 PR=2 LTA=3 SO=4
         source    TYPE char3,
         docno     TYPE char10,
         doctype   TYPE char4,
         erdat     TYPE erdat,
         ernam     TYPE ernam,
         frggr     TYPE ekko-frggr,
         frgsx     TYPE ekko-frgsx,
         frgke     TYPE ekko-frgke,
         frgzu     TYPE ekko-frgzu,
         rel_level TYPE char2,
         uname     TYPE cdhdr-username,
         fullname  TYPE user_addr-name_textc,
         udate     TYPE cdhdr-udate,
         utime     TYPE cdhdr-utime,
         objcl     TYPE cdhdr-objectclas,    " helper (hidden)
         objid     TYPE cdhdr-objectid,      " helper (hidden)
       END OF ty_out.

Step 2: Selection screen

Fields appear or disappear depending on the radio button:

AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT.
  LOOP AT SCREEN.
    CASE screen-group1.
      WHEN 'PO'.
        IF r_po = 'X'. screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
      WHEN 'PR'.
        IF r_pr = 'X'. screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
      WHEN 'LTA'.
        IF r_lta = 'X'. screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
      WHEN 'SO'.
        IF r_so = 'X'. screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
    ENDCASE.
    MODIFY SCREEN.
  ENDLOOP.

Step 3: Read the starting documents.

WHEN r_po.
  SELECT ebeln, bsart, aedat, ernam, frggr, frgsx, frgke, frgzu
    FROM ekko
    WHERE ebeln IN @s_ebeln
      AND aedat IN @s_aedat
      AND bsart IN @s_bsart
      AND bstyp = 'F'
    INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_po).

PR, LTA and SO follow the same pattern, using EBAN, EKKO (bstyp K or L) and VBAK.
Step 4: Release history

SELECT objectclas, objectid, changenr, username, udate, utime
  FROM cdhdr
  FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_keys
  WHERE objectclas = @LT_keys-objectclas
    AND objectid   = @LT_keys-objectid
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_hdr).

SELECT objectclas, objectid, changenr, tabname, fname, value_new
  FROM cdpos
  FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_hdr
  WHERE objectclas = @LT_hdr-objectclas
    AND objectid   = @LT_hdr-objectid
    AND changenr   = @LT_hdr-changenr
    AND tabname   IN ('EKKO', 'EBAN')
    AND fname      = 'FRGZU'
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_pos).

The release level is the number of X characters in the new status:

lv_cnt = count( val = ls_pos-value_new sub = 'X' ).
IF lv_cnt > 0.
  ls_final-rel_level = |{ lv_cnt }|.
ENDIF.

Step 5: Find linked documents

From	To	Link
PO	PR	EKPO-BANFN
PO or PR	LTA	EKPO-KONNR, EBAN-KONNR
LTA or PO	SO	EKKN-VBELN
PR	SO	EBKN-VBELN, VBEP-BANFN
" PO -> PR
SELECT DISTINCT banfn FROM ekpo
  WHERE ebeln = @PV_docno
    AND banfn <> @Space
  APPENDING TABLE @LT_prs.

" keep only real agreements (contract K / scheduling agreement L)
SELECT ebeln FROM ekko
  FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_cand
  WHERE ebeln = @LT_cand-table_line
    AND bstyp IN ('K', 'L')
  INTO TABLE @LT_ltas.

Step 6: ALV with hotspots:

cl_salv_table=>factory( IMPORTING r_salv_table = go_alv
                        CHANGING  t_table      = gt_out ).

" DOCNO = go down one level
lo_col_tab ?= lo_cols->get_column( 'DOCNO' ).
lo_col_tab->set_cell_type( if_salv_c_cell_type=>hotspot ).

" SOURCE = go back one level
lo_col_tab ?= lo_cols->get_column( 'SOURCE' ).
lo_col_tab->set_cell_type( if_salv_c_cell_type=>hotspot ).

" hide helper columns
lo_cols->get_column( 'OBJCL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).
lo_cols->get_column( 'OBJID' )->set_visible( abap_false ).
lo_cols->get_column( 'LVL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).

SET HANDLER go_handler->on_link_click FOR lo_events.

Step 7: Click handler

METHOD on_link_click.
  CASE column.
    WHEN 'DOCNO'.  PERFORM do_drill USING row.
    WHEN 'SOURCE'. PERFORM do_back.
  ENDCASE.
ENDMETHOD.

Step 8: Drill down (one level per click)

CASE ls_row-source.
  WHEN 'PO'.  lv_next = 'PR'.
  WHEN 'PR'.  lv_next = 'LTA'.
  WHEN 'LTA'. lv_next = 'SO'.
ENDCASE.

PERFORM get_chain USING    ls_row-source ls_row-docno
                  CHANGING lt_new lv_dummy.
DELETE lt_new WHERE source <> lv_next.     " keep ONLY the next level

" remember the current level
ls_hist-title = gv_title.
ls_hist-data  = gt_out.
APPEND ls_hist TO gt_hist.

" show the next level in the SAME alv
gt_out   = lt_new.
gv_title = lv_title.
PERFORM refresh_alv.

Step 9: Refresh the same ALV:

FORM refresh_alv.
  go_alv->get_display_settings( )->set_list_header( gv_title ).
  go_alv->get_columns( )->set_optimize( abap_true ).
  go_alv->refresh( ).
ENDFORM.

Step:10  Display

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&      Form  DISPLAY_ALV  (single full-screen ALV, no popup)
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM display_alv.

  DATA: lo_cols    TYPE REF TO cl_salv_columns_table,
        lo_col_tab TYPE REF TO cl_salv_column_table,
        lo_events  TYPE REF TO cl_salv_events_table.

  IF gt_out IS INITIAL.
    MESSAGE 'No data found for the given selection' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'W'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  TRY.
      cl_salv_table=>factory( IMPORTING r_salv_table = go_alv
                              CHANGING  t_table      = gt_out ).

      go_alv->get_functions( )->set_all( abap_true ).
      go_alv->get_display_settings( )->set_list_header( gv_title ).
      go_alv->get_display_settings( )->set_striped_pattern( abap_true ).

      lo_cols = go_alv->get_columns( ).
      lo_cols->set_optimize( abap_true ).

      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'SOURCE'    'Source'     'Source'         'Source'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'DOCNO'     'Document'   'Document No.'   'Document Number'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'DOCTYPE'   'Doc.Type'   'Doc. Type'      'Document Type'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'ERDAT'     'Created On' 'Created On'     'Created On'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'ERNAM'     'Created By' 'Created By'     'Created By'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGGR'     'Rel.Group'  'Release Group'  'Release Group'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGSX'     'Rel.Strat.' 'Rel. Strategy'  'Release Strategy'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGKE'     'Rel.Ind.'   'Rel. Indicator' 'Release Indicator'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGZU'     'Rel.Status' 'Release Status' 'Release Status'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'REL_LEVEL' 'Rel.Level'  'Release Level'  'Release Level'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'UNAME'     'User ID'    'User ID'        'User ID'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FULLNAME'  'Full Name'  'Full Name'      'Full Name'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'UDATE'     'Rel.Date'   'Release Date'   'Release Date'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'UTIME'     'Rel.Time'   'Release Time'   'Release Time'.

      " hide helper columns
      lo_cols->get_column( 'OBJCL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).
      lo_cols->get_column( 'OBJID' )->set_visible( abap_false ).
      lo_cols->get_column( 'LVL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).

      " DOCNO  = hotspot: go DOWN one level
      lo_col_tab ?= lo_cols->get_column( 'DOCNO' ).
      lo_col_tab->set_cell_type( if_salv_c_cell_type=>hotspot ).

      " SOURCE = hotspot: go BACK one level
      lo_col_tab ?= lo_cols->get_column( 'SOURCE' ).
      lo_col_tab->set_cell_type( if_salv_c_cell_type=>hotspot ).

      lo_events = go_alv->get_event( ).
      CREATE OBJECT go_handler.
      SET HANDLER go_handler->on_link_click FOR lo_events.

      go_alv->display( ).

    CATCH cx_salv_msg cx_salv_not_found cx_salv_data_error INTO DATA(lx).
      MESSAGE lx->get_text( ) TYPE 'E'.
  ENDTRY.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&      Form  SET_COL  -  column headings
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM set_col USING po_cols  TYPE REF TO cl_salv_columns_table
                   pv_name
                   pv_short
                   pv_med
                   pv_long.

  DATA: lo_col   TYPE REF TO cl_salv_column,
        lv_name  TYPE lvc_fname,
        lv_short TYPE scrtext_s,
        lv_med   TYPE scrtext_m,
        lv_long  TYPE scrtext_l.

  lv_name  = pv_name.
  lv_short = pv_short.
  lv_med   = pv_med.
  lv_long  = pv_long.

  TRY.
      lo_col = po_cols->get_column( lv_name ).
      lo_col->set_short_text( lv_short ).
      lo_col->set_medium_text( lv_med ).
      lo_col->set_long_text( lv_long ).
    CATCH cx_salv_not_found.
  ENDTRY.



Full Report

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Report  ZPO_RELEASE_AUDIT
*& PO Release Audit Report
*&   Same-ALV drill-down, ONE level per click (no popup)
*&   Click PO  document no. -> PR records
*&   Click PR  document no. -> LTA records
*&   Click LTA document no. -> SO records
*&   Click SOURCE           -> go back one level
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
REPORT zpo_release_audit.

TABLES: ekko, eban, vbak.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* Types and data
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_out,
         lvl       TYPE n LENGTH 1,            " helper: PO=1 PR=2 LTA=3 SO=4
         source    TYPE char3,
         docno     TYPE char10,
         doctype   TYPE char4,
         erdat     TYPE erdat,
         ernam     TYPE ernam,
         frggr     TYPE ekko-frggr,
         frgsx     TYPE ekko-frgsx,
         frgke     TYPE ekko-frgke,
         frgzu     TYPE ekko-frgzu,
         rel_level TYPE char2,
         uname     TYPE cdhdr-username,
         fullname  TYPE user_addr-name_textc,
         udate     TYPE cdhdr-udate,
         utime     TYPE cdhdr-utime,
         objcl     TYPE cdhdr-objectclas,
         objid     TYPE cdhdr-objectid,
       END OF ty_out.

TYPES tt_out TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_out WITH DEFAULT KEY.
TYPES tt_num TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF char10 WITH DEFAULT KEY.

" history of previous levels (for going back)
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_hist,
         title TYPE lvc_title,
         data  TYPE tt_out,
       END OF ty_hist.

DATA: gt_out   TYPE tt_out,                    " data shown in the ALV
      gs_out   TYPE ty_out,
      gv_year  TYPE gjahr,
      gv_title TYPE lvc_title,                 " current ALV header
      gt_hist  TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_hist, " previous levels
      go_alv   TYPE REF TO cl_salv_table.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* ALV hotspot handler
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
CLASS lcl_handler DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS on_link_click
      FOR EVENT link_click OF cl_salv_events_table
      IMPORTING row column.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_handler IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD on_link_click.
    CASE column.
      WHEN 'DOCNO'.
        PERFORM do_drill USING row.
      WHEN 'SOURCE'.
        PERFORM do_back.
    ENDCASE.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

DATA go_handler TYPE REF TO lcl_handler.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* Selection screen
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b1 WITH FRAME.
  SELECT-OPTIONS: s_year  FOR gv_year,                    "Year (always)
                  s_ebeln FOR ekko-ebeln MODIF ID po,     "Purchasing Document
                  s_aedat FOR ekko-aedat,                 "Created On (always)
                  s_bsart FOR ekko-bsart MODIF ID dty,    "Doc. Type
                  s_banfn FOR eban-banfn MODIF ID pr,     "Purchase Requisition
                  s_lta   FOR ekko-ebeln MODIF ID lta,    "Long Term Agreement
                  s_vbeln FOR vbak-vbeln MODIF ID so.     "Sales Order
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b1.

SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b2 WITH FRAME.
  PARAMETERS: r_po  RADIOBUTTON GROUP g1 DEFAULT 'X' USER-COMMAND uc1,
              r_pr  RADIOBUTTON GROUP g1,
              r_lta RADIOBUTTON GROUP g1,
              r_so  RADIOBUTTON GROUP g1.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b2.

SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b3 WITH FRAME.
  PARAMETERS: p_po  AS CHECKBOX DEFAULT 'X' MODIF ID chk,
              p_pr  AS CHECKBOX DEFAULT 'X' MODIF ID chk,
              p_so  AS CHECKBOX DEFAULT 'X' MODIF ID chk,
              p_lta AS CHECKBOX DEFAULT 'X' MODIF ID chk.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b3.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* Initialization: field texts and default year range
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
INITIALIZATION.
  %_s_year_%_app_%-text  = 'Year'.
  %_s_ebeln_%_app_%-text = 'Purchasing Document'.
  %_s_aedat_%_app_%-text = 'Created On'.
  %_s_bsart_%_app_%-text = 'Purchasing Doc. Type'.
  %_s_banfn_%_app_%-text = 'Purchase Requisition'.
  %_s_lta_%_app_%-text   = 'Long Term Agreement'.
  %_s_vbeln_%_app_%-text = 'Sales Order'.
  %_r_po_%_app_%-text    = 'PO Selection'.
  %_r_pr_%_app_%-text    = 'PR Selection'.
  %_r_lta_%_app_%-text   = 'LTA Selection'.
  %_r_so_%_app_%-text    = 'SO Selection'.
  %_p_po_%_app_%-text    = 'PO'.
  %_p_pr_%_app_%-text    = 'PR'.
  %_p_so_%_app_%-text    = 'SO'.
  %_p_lta_%_app_%-text   = 'LTA'.

  s_year-sign   = 'I'.
  s_year-option = 'BT'.
  s_year-low    = '2023'.
  s_year-high   = '2026'.
  APPEND s_year.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* When a radio button is clicked: reset all checkboxes to ticked.
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
AT SELECTION-SCREEN.
  IF sy-ucomm = 'UC1'.
    p_po  = 'X'.
    p_pr  = 'X'.
    p_so  = 'X'.
    p_lta = 'X'.
  ENDIF.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* Dynamic screen handling
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT.

  LOOP AT SCREEN.

    CASE screen-group1.
      WHEN 'PO'.
        IF r_po = 'X'.  screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
      WHEN 'PR'.
        IF r_pr = 'X'.  screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
      WHEN 'LTA'.
        IF r_lta = 'X'. screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
      WHEN 'SO'.
        IF r_so = 'X'.  screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
      WHEN 'DTY'.                          " doc type not used for SO
        IF r_so = 'X'.  screen-active = 0. ELSE. screen-active = 1. ENDIF.
    ENDCASE.

    IF screen-group1 = 'CHK'.
      IF screen-name CS 'P_SO'.
        IF r_po = 'X' OR r_so = 'X'.
          screen-active = 1.
        ELSE.
          screen-active = 0.
        ENDIF.
      ELSEIF screen-name CS 'P_LTA'.
        IF r_po = 'X' OR r_lta = 'X'.
          screen-active = 1.
        ELSE.
          screen-active = 0.
        ENDIF.
      ELSE.
        screen-active = 1.
      ENDIF.
      screen-input = 1.
    ENDIF.

    MODIFY SCREEN.
  ENDLOOP.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* Main processing
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
START-OF-SELECTION.
  PERFORM get_data.

  IF p_po  IS INITIAL. DELETE gt_out WHERE source = 'PO'.  ENDIF.
  IF p_pr  IS INITIAL. DELETE gt_out WHERE source = 'PR'.  ENDIF.
  IF p_so  IS INITIAL. DELETE gt_out WHERE source = 'SO'.  ENDIF.
  IF p_lta IS INITIAL. DELETE gt_out WHERE source = 'LTA'. ENDIF.

  PERFORM filter_year.
  PERFORM get_release_history CHANGING gt_out.

  gv_title = 'PO Release Audit Report'.
  PERFORM display_alv.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&      Form  GET_DATA
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM get_data.

  CASE 'X'.

    WHEN r_po.                                   " ---- Purchase Orders
      SELECT ebeln, bsart, aedat, ernam, frggr, frgsx, frgke, frgzu
        FROM ekko
        WHERE ebeln IN @s_ebeln
          AND aedat IN @s_aedat
          AND bsart IN @s_bsart
          AND bstyp = 'F'
        INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_po).

      LOOP AT lt_po INTO DATA(ls_po).
        CLEAR gs_out.
        gs_out-source  = 'PO'.
        gs_out-objcl   = 'EINKBELEG'.
        gs_out-docno   = ls_po-ebeln.
        gs_out-objid   = ls_po-ebeln.
        gs_out-doctype = ls_po-bsart.
        gs_out-erdat   = ls_po-aedat.
        gs_out-ernam   = ls_po-ernam.
        gs_out-frggr   = ls_po-frggr.
        gs_out-frgsx   = ls_po-frgsx.
        gs_out-frgke   = ls_po-frgke.
        gs_out-frgzu   = ls_po-frgzu.
        APPEND gs_out TO gt_out.
      ENDLOOP.

    WHEN r_pr.                                   " ---- Purchase Requisitions
      SELECT DISTINCT banfn, bsart, erdat, ernam, frggr, frgst, frgkz, frgzu
        FROM eban
        WHERE banfn IN @s_banfn
          AND erdat IN @s_aedat
          AND bsart IN @s_bsart
        INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_pr).

      LOOP AT lt_pr INTO DATA(ls_pr).
        CLEAR gs_out.
        gs_out-source  = 'PR'.
        gs_out-objcl   = 'BANF'.
        gs_out-docno   = ls_pr-banfn.
        gs_out-objid   = ls_pr-banfn.
        gs_out-doctype = ls_pr-bsart.
        gs_out-erdat   = ls_pr-erdat.
        gs_out-ernam   = ls_pr-ernam.
        gs_out-frggr   = ls_pr-frggr.
        gs_out-frgsx   = ls_pr-frgst.
        gs_out-frgke   = ls_pr-frgkz.
        gs_out-frgzu   = ls_pr-frgzu.
        APPEND gs_out TO gt_out.
      ENDLOOP.

    WHEN r_lta.                                  " ---- Long Term Agreements
      SELECT ebeln, bsart, aedat, ernam, frggr, frgsx, frgke, frgzu
        FROM ekko
        WHERE ebeln IN @s_lta
          AND aedat IN @s_aedat
          AND bsart IN @s_bsart
          AND bstyp IN ('K', 'L')
        INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_lta).

      LOOP AT lt_lta INTO DATA(ls_lta).
        CLEAR gs_out.
        gs_out-source  = 'LTA'.
        gs_out-objcl   = 'EINKBELEG'.
        gs_out-docno   = ls_lta-ebeln.
        gs_out-objid   = ls_lta-ebeln.
        gs_out-doctype = ls_lta-bsart.
        gs_out-erdat   = ls_lta-aedat.
        gs_out-ernam   = ls_lta-ernam.
        gs_out-frggr   = ls_lta-frggr.
        gs_out-frgsx   = ls_lta-frgsx.
        gs_out-frgke   = ls_lta-frgke.
        gs_out-frgzu   = ls_lta-frgzu.
        APPEND gs_out TO gt_out.
      ENDLOOP.

    WHEN r_so.                                   " ---- Sales Orders
      SELECT vbeln, auart, erdat, ernam
        FROM vbak
        WHERE vbeln IN @s_vbeln
          AND erdat IN @s_aedat
        INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_so).

      LOOP AT lt_so INTO DATA(ls_so).
        CLEAR gs_out.
        gs_out-source  = 'SO'.
        gs_out-objcl   = 'VERKBELEG'.
        gs_out-docno   = ls_so-vbeln.
        gs_out-objid   = ls_so-vbeln.
        gs_out-doctype = ls_so-auart.
        gs_out-erdat   = ls_so-erdat.
        gs_out-ernam   = ls_so-ernam.
        APPEND gs_out TO gt_out.
      ENDLOOP.

  ENDCASE.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&      Form  FILTER_YEAR
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM filter_year.

  DATA: ls_row  TYPE ty_out,
        lv_year TYPE gjahr.

  LOOP AT gt_out INTO ls_row.
    lv_year = ls_row-erdat(4).
    IF lv_year NOT IN s_year.
      DELETE gt_out INDEX sy-tabix.
    ENDIF.
  ENDLOOP.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&      Form  GET_RELEASE_HISTORY
*&  Release level, user id, full name, date, time from change documents
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM get_release_history CHANGING ct_out TYPE tt_out.

  TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_key,
           objectclas TYPE cdhdr-objectclas,
           objectid   TYPE cdhdr-objectid,
         END OF ty_key.

  DATA: lt_keys  TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_key,
        ls_key   TYPE ty_key,
        ls_out   TYPE ty_out,
        lt_final TYPE tt_out,
        ls_final TYPE ty_out,
        lv_found TYPE abap_bool,
        lv_cnt   TYPE i.

  FIELD-SYMBOLS <ls_f> TYPE ty_out.

  CHECK ct_out IS NOT INITIAL.

  LOOP AT ct_out INTO ls_out WHERE source <> 'SO'.
    ls_key-objectclas = ls_out-objcl.
    ls_key-objectid   = ls_out-objid.
    APPEND ls_key TO lt_keys.
  ENDLOOP.
  SORT lt_keys BY objectclas objectid.
  DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_keys COMPARING objectclas objectid.

  IF lt_keys IS NOT INITIAL.

    SELECT objectclas, objectid, changenr, username, udate, utime
      FROM cdhdr
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_keys
      WHERE objectclas = @LT_keys-objectclas
        AND objectid   = @LT_keys-objectid
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_hdr).

    IF lt_hdr IS NOT INITIAL.

      SELECT objectclas, objectid, changenr, tabname, fname, value_new
        FROM cdpos
        FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_hdr
        WHERE objectclas = @LT_hdr-objectclas
          AND objectid   = @LT_hdr-objectid
          AND changenr   = @LT_hdr-changenr
          AND tabname   IN ('EKKO', 'EBAN')
          AND fname      = 'FRGZU'
        INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_pos).

      SORT lt_pos BY objectclas objectid changenr value_new.
      DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_pos
             COMPARING objectclas objectid changenr value_new.

      SELECT bname, name_textc
        FROM user_addr
        FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_hdr
        WHERE bname = @LT_hdr-username
        INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_name).

      SORT lt_hdr  BY objectclas objectid changenr.
      SORT lt_name BY bname.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

  LOOP AT ct_out INTO ls_out.

    lv_found = abap_false.

    LOOP AT lt_pos INTO DATA(ls_pos)
         WHERE objectclas = ls_out-objcl
           AND objectid   = ls_out-objid.

      READ TABLE lt_hdr INTO DATA(ls_hdr)
           WITH KEY objectclas = ls_pos-objectclas
                    objectid   = ls_pos-objectid
                    changenr   = ls_pos-changenr
           BINARY SEARCH.
      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        CONTINUE.
      ENDIF.

      ls_final        = ls_out.
      ls_final-uname  = ls_hdr-username.
      ls_final-udate  = ls_hdr-udate.
      ls_final-utime  = ls_hdr-utime.
      ls_final-frgzu  = ls_pos-value_new.

      lv_cnt = count( val = ls_pos-value_new sub = 'X' ).
      IF lv_cnt > 0.
        ls_final-rel_level = |{ lv_cnt }|.
      ENDIF.

      READ TABLE lt_name INTO DATA(ls_name)
           WITH KEY bname = ls_hdr-username BINARY SEARCH.
      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        ls_final-fullname = ls_name-name_textc.
      ENDIF.

      APPEND ls_final TO lt_final.
      lv_found = abap_true.
    ENDLOOP.

    IF lv_found = abap_false.
      APPEND ls_out TO lt_final.
    ENDIF.

  ENDLOOP.

  ct_out = lt_final.

  LOOP AT ct_out ASSIGNING <ls_f>.
    CASE <ls_f>-source.
      WHEN 'PO'.  <ls_f>-lvl = 1.
      WHEN 'PR'.  <ls_f>-lvl = 2.
      WHEN 'LTA'. <ls_f>-lvl = 3.
      WHEN 'SO'.  <ls_f>-lvl = 4.
    ENDCASE.
  ENDLOOP.

  SORT ct_out BY lvl docno udate utime.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&  GET_CHAIN : finds PO / PR / LTA / SO linked to the clicked row
*&  (do_drill keeps only the next level)
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM get_chain USING    pv_source TYPE char3
                        pv_docno  TYPE char10
               CHANGING ct_det    TYPE tt_out
                        cv_title  TYPE lvc_title.

  DATA: lt_pos  TYPE tt_num,    " POs shown in the list
        lt_rel  TYPE tt_num,    " related POs (only used to find links)
        lt_prs  TYPE tt_num,    " PRs
        lt_cand TYPE tt_num,    " LTA candidates
        lt_ltas TYPE tt_num,    " real LTAs
        lt_sos  TYPE tt_num.    " SOs

  CLEAR: ct_det, cv_title.

  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  " 1) Starting point
  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  CASE pv_source.

    WHEN 'PO'.
      APPEND pv_docno TO lt_pos.
      APPEND pv_docno TO lt_rel.

      " PO -> PR (PO items)
      SELECT DISTINCT banfn FROM ekpo
        WHERE ebeln = @PV_docno
          AND banfn <> @Space
        APPENDING TABLE @LT_prs.

    WHEN 'PR'.
      APPEND pv_docno TO lt_prs.

    WHEN 'LTA'.
      APPEND pv_docno TO lt_cand.

      " POs that reference this LTA (used to find sales orders)
      SELECT DISTINCT ebeln FROM ekpo
        WHERE konnr = @PV_docno
        APPENDING TABLE @LT_rel.

  ENDCASE.

  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  " 2) PR -> related POs and LTA candidates
  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  IF lt_prs IS NOT INITIAL.
    SORT lt_prs.
    DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_prs.

    " POs created from the PR
    SELECT ebeln FROM ekpo
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_prs
      WHERE banfn = @LT_prs-table_line
      APPENDING TABLE @LT_rel.

    " PO / agreement number stored on the PR
    SELECT ebeln FROM eban
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_prs
      WHERE banfn = @LT_prs-table_line
        AND ebeln <> @Space
      APPENDING TABLE @LT_rel.

    " agreement number entered on the PR
    SELECT konnr FROM eban
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_prs
      WHERE banfn = @LT_prs-table_line
        AND konnr <> @Space
      APPENDING TABLE @LT_cand.
  ENDIF.

  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  " 3) related POs -> agreement referenced on PO items
  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  IF lt_rel IS NOT INITIAL.
    SORT lt_rel.
    DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_rel.

    SELECT konnr FROM ekpo
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_rel
      WHERE ebeln = @LT_rel-table_line
        AND konnr <> @Space
      APPENDING TABLE @LT_cand.

    " scheduling agreements may be linked directly (EBELN)
    APPEND LINES OF lt_rel TO lt_cand.
  ENDIF.

  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  " 4) keep only real agreements (contract K / scheduling agreement L)
  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  SORT lt_cand.
  DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_cand.
  DELETE lt_cand WHERE table_line IS INITIAL.

  IF lt_cand IS NOT INITIAL.
    SELECT ebeln FROM ekko
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_cand
      WHERE ebeln = @LT_cand-table_line
        AND bstyp IN ('K', 'L')
      INTO TABLE @LT_ltas.
  ENDIF.

  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  " 5) Sales orders
  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  " LTA account assignment
  IF lt_ltas IS NOT INITIAL.
    SELECT vbeln FROM ekkn
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_ltas
      WHERE ebeln = @LT_ltas-table_line
        AND vbeln <> @Space
      APPENDING TABLE @LT_sos.
  ENDIF.

  " PO account assignment
  IF lt_rel IS NOT INITIAL.
    SELECT vbeln FROM ekkn
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_rel
      WHERE ebeln = @LT_rel-table_line
        AND vbeln <> @Space
      APPENDING TABLE @LT_sos.
  ENDIF.

  " PR account assignment and SO schedule lines (third-party items)
  IF lt_prs IS NOT INITIAL.
    SELECT vbeln FROM ebkn
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_prs
      WHERE banfn = @LT_prs-table_line
        AND vbeln <> @Space
      APPENDING TABLE @LT_sos.

    SELECT vbeln FROM vbep
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_prs
      WHERE banfn = @LT_prs-table_line
      APPENDING TABLE @LT_sos.
  ENDIF.

  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  " 6) Build output rows: PO, PR, LTA, SO
  "------------------------------------------------------------------
  PERFORM add_ekko USING 'PO'  lt_pos  CHANGING ct_det.
  PERFORM add_eban USING       lt_prs  CHANGING ct_det.
  PERFORM add_ekko USING 'LTA' lt_ltas CHANGING ct_det.
  PERFORM add_vbak USING       lt_sos  CHANGING ct_det.

  " only the clicked document itself found = nothing linked
  IF lines( ct_det ) <= 1.
    CLEAR ct_det.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  cv_title = |Linked documents for { pv_source } { pv_docno }|.

  " release level, user id, full name, date, time for every row
  PERFORM get_release_history CHANGING ct_det.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&  ADD_EKKO : PO rows (pv_source = PO) or LTA rows (pv_source = LTA)
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM add_ekko USING    pv_source TYPE char3
                       pt_nums   TYPE tt_num
              CHANGING ct_det    TYPE tt_out.

  DATA: lt_n     TYPE tt_num,
        lr_bstyp TYPE RANGE OF ekko-bstyp,
        ls_det   TYPE ty_out.

  lt_n = pt_nums.
  SORT lt_n.
  DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_n.
  DELETE lt_n WHERE table_line IS INITIAL.
  IF lt_n IS INITIAL.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  IF pv_source = 'PO'.
    lr_bstyp = VALUE #( ( sign = 'I' option = 'EQ' low = 'F' ) ).
  ELSE.
    lr_bstyp = VALUE #( ( sign = 'I' option = 'EQ' low = 'K' )
                        ( sign = 'I' option = 'EQ' low = 'L' ) ).
  ENDIF.

  SELECT ebeln, bsart, aedat, ernam, frggr, frgsx, frgke, frgzu
    FROM ekko
    FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_n
    WHERE ebeln = @LT_n-table_line
      AND bstyp IN @LR_bstyp
    INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_ekko).

  SORT lt_ekko BY ebeln.

  LOOP AT lt_ekko INTO DATA(ls_ekko).
    CLEAR ls_det.
    ls_det-source  = pv_source.
    ls_det-objcl   = 'EINKBELEG'.
    ls_det-docno   = ls_ekko-ebeln.
    ls_det-objid   = ls_ekko-ebeln.
    ls_det-doctype = ls_ekko-bsart.
    ls_det-erdat   = ls_ekko-aedat.
    ls_det-ernam   = ls_ekko-ernam.
    ls_det-frggr   = ls_ekko-frggr.
    ls_det-frgsx   = ls_ekko-frgsx.
    ls_det-frgke   = ls_ekko-frgke.
    ls_det-frgzu   = ls_ekko-frgzu.
    APPEND ls_det TO ct_det.
  ENDLOOP.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&  ADD_EBAN : PR rows
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM add_eban USING    pt_nums TYPE tt_num
              CHANGING ct_det  TYPE tt_out.

  DATA: lt_n   TYPE tt_num,
        ls_det TYPE ty_out.

  lt_n = pt_nums.
  SORT lt_n.
  DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_n.
  DELETE lt_n WHERE table_line IS INITIAL.
  IF lt_n IS INITIAL.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  SELECT banfn, bsart, erdat, ernam, frggr, frgst, frgkz, frgzu
    FROM eban
    FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_n
    WHERE banfn = @LT_n-table_line
    INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_eban).

  SORT lt_eban BY banfn.
  DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_eban COMPARING banfn.

  LOOP AT lt_eban INTO DATA(ls_eban).
    CLEAR ls_det.
    ls_det-source  = 'PR'.
    ls_det-objcl   = 'BANF'.
    ls_det-docno   = ls_eban-banfn.
    ls_det-objid   = ls_eban-banfn.
    ls_det-doctype = ls_eban-bsart.
    ls_det-erdat   = ls_eban-erdat.
    ls_det-ernam   = ls_eban-ernam.
    ls_det-frggr   = ls_eban-frggr.
    ls_det-frgsx   = ls_eban-frgst.
    ls_det-frgke   = ls_eban-frgkz.
    ls_det-frgzu   = ls_eban-frgzu.
    APPEND ls_det TO ct_det.
  ENDLOOP.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&  ADD_VBAK : SO rows
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM add_vbak USING    pt_nums TYPE tt_num
              CHANGING ct_det  TYPE tt_out.

  DATA: lt_n   TYPE tt_num,
        ls_det TYPE ty_out.

  lt_n = pt_nums.
  SORT lt_n.
  DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_n.
  DELETE lt_n WHERE table_line IS INITIAL.
  IF lt_n IS INITIAL.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  SELECT vbeln, auart, erdat, ernam
    FROM vbak
    FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT_n
    WHERE vbeln = @LT_n-table_line
    INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_vbak).

  SORT lt_vbak BY vbeln.

  LOOP AT lt_vbak INTO DATA(ls_vbak).
    CLEAR ls_det.
    ls_det-source  = 'SO'.
    ls_det-objcl   = 'VERKBELEG'.
    ls_det-docno   = ls_vbak-vbeln.
    ls_det-objid   = ls_vbak-vbeln.
    ls_det-doctype = ls_vbak-auart.
    ls_det-erdat   = ls_vbak-erdat.
    ls_det-ernam   = ls_vbak-ernam.
    APPEND ls_det TO ct_det.
  ENDLOOP.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&  DO_DRILL : click on Document No.
*&     PO  -> only PR rows
*&     PR  -> only LTA rows
*&     LTA -> only SO rows
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM do_drill USING pv_row TYPE i.

  DATA: ls_row   TYPE ty_out,
        lt_new   TYPE tt_out,
        lv_title TYPE lvc_title,
        lv_next  TYPE char3,
        ls_hist  TYPE ty_hist,
        lv_cnt   TYPE i.
data:        lv_dummy TYPE lvc_title.
  READ TABLE gt_out INTO ls_row INDEX pv_row.
  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  IF ls_row-source = 'SO'.
    MESSAGE 'No further details below Sales Order' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'W'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  " which level should be shown next
  CASE ls_row-source.
    WHEN 'PO'.
      lv_next  = 'PR'.
      lv_title = |PR details for PO { ls_row-docno }|.
    WHEN 'PR'.
      lv_next  = 'LTA'.
      lv_title = |LTA details for PR { ls_row-docno }|.
    WHEN 'LTA'.
      lv_next  = 'SO'.
      lv_title = |SO details for LTA { ls_row-docno }|.
  ENDCASE.

  " find all linked documents, then keep ONLY the next level
    PERFORM get_chain USING    ls_row-source ls_row-docno
                    CHANGING lt_new lv_dummy.
  DELETE lt_new WHERE source <> lv_next.

  IF lt_new IS INITIAL.
    MESSAGE |No { lv_next } found for { ls_row-source } { ls_row-docno }|
            TYPE 'I'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  " remember the current level so we can come back
  ls_hist-title = gv_title.
  ls_hist-data  = gt_out.
  APPEND ls_hist TO gt_hist.

  " show the next level in the SAME alv
  gt_out   = lt_new.
  gv_title = lv_title.
  PERFORM refresh_alv.

  lv_cnt = lines( lt_new ).
  MESSAGE |{ lv_cnt } { lv_next } record(s) found| TYPE 'S'.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&  DO_BACK : click on Source -> go back to the previous level
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM do_back.

  DATA lv_lines TYPE i.
  FIELD-SYMBOLS <ls_hist> TYPE ty_hist.

  lv_lines = lines( gt_hist ).
  IF lv_lines = 0.
    MESSAGE 'You are already at the first level' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'W'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  READ TABLE gt_hist ASSIGNING <ls_hist> INDEX lv_lines.
  gt_out   = <ls_hist>-data.
  gv_title = <ls_hist>-title.
  DELETE gt_hist INDEX lv_lines.

  PERFORM refresh_alv.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&  REFRESH_ALV : reload the changed GT_OUT into the same ALV
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM refresh_alv.

  go_alv->get_display_settings( )->set_list_header( gv_title ).
  go_alv->get_columns( )->set_optimize( abap_true ).
  go_alv->refresh( ).

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&      Form  DISPLAY_ALV  (single full-screen ALV, no popup)
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM display_alv.

  DATA: lo_cols    TYPE REF TO cl_salv_columns_table,
        lo_col_tab TYPE REF TO cl_salv_column_table,
        lo_events  TYPE REF TO cl_salv_events_table.

  IF gt_out IS INITIAL.
    MESSAGE 'No data found for the given selection' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'W'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  TRY.
      cl_salv_table=>factory( IMPORTING r_salv_table = go_alv
                              CHANGING  t_table      = gt_out ).

      go_alv->get_functions( )->set_all( abap_true ).
      go_alv->get_display_settings( )->set_list_header( gv_title ).
      go_alv->get_display_settings( )->set_striped_pattern( abap_true ).

      lo_cols = go_alv->get_columns( ).
      lo_cols->set_optimize( abap_true ).

      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'SOURCE'    'Source'     'Source'         'Source'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'DOCNO'     'Document'   'Document No.'   'Document Number'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'DOCTYPE'   'Doc.Type'   'Doc. Type'      'Document Type'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'ERDAT'     'Created On' 'Created On'     'Created On'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'ERNAM'     'Created By' 'Created By'     'Created By'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGGR'     'Rel.Group'  'Release Group'  'Release Group'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGSX'     'Rel.Strat.' 'Rel. Strategy'  'Release Strategy'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGKE'     'Rel.Ind.'   'Rel. Indicator' 'Release Indicator'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGZU'     'Rel.Status' 'Release Status' 'Release Status'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'REL_LEVEL' 'Rel.Level'  'Release Level'  'Release Level'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'UNAME'     'User ID'    'User ID'        'User ID'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FULLNAME'  'Full Name'  'Full Name'      'Full Name'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'UDATE'     'Rel.Date'   'Release Date'   'Release Date'.
      PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'UTIME'     'Rel.Time'   'Release Time'   'Release Time'.

      " hide helper columns
      lo_cols->get_column( 'OBJCL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).
      lo_cols->get_column( 'OBJID' )->set_visible( abap_false ).
      lo_cols->get_column( 'LVL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).

      " DOCNO  = hotspot: go DOWN one level
      lo_col_tab ?= lo_cols->get_column( 'DOCNO' ).
      lo_col_tab->set_cell_type( if_salv_c_cell_type=>hotspot ).

      " SOURCE = hotspot: go BACK one level
      lo_col_tab ?= lo_cols->get_column( 'SOURCE' ).
      lo_col_tab->set_cell_type( if_salv_c_cell_type=>hotspot ).

      lo_events = go_alv->get_event( ).
      CREATE OBJECT go_handler.
      SET HANDLER go_handler->on_link_click FOR lo_events.

      go_alv->display( ).

    CATCH cx_salv_msg cx_salv_not_found cx_salv_data_error INTO DATA(lx).
      MESSAGE lx->get_text( ) TYPE 'E'.
  ENDTRY.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*&      Form  SET_COL  -  column headings
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM set_col USING po_cols  TYPE REF TO cl_salv_columns_table
                   pv_name
                   pv_short
                   pv_med
                   pv_long.

  DATA: lo_col   TYPE REF TO cl_salv_column,
        lv_name  TYPE lvc_fname,
        lv_short TYPE scrtext_s,
        lv_med   TYPE scrtext_m,
        lv_long  TYPE scrtext_l.

  lv_name  = pv_name.
  lv_short = pv_short.
  lv_med   = pv_med.
  lv_long  = pv_long.

  TRY.
      lo_col = po_cols->get_column( lv_name ).
      lo_col->set_short_text( lv_short ).
      lo_col->set_medium_text( lv_med ).
      lo_col->set_long_text( lv_long ).
    CATCH cx_salv_not_found.
  ENDTRY.

ENDFORM.

 

What the user gets
                Column                                                                         Meaning
Source / Document No.                                          Document type and number (clickable)
Release Group, Strategy, Indicator, Status        Current release data
Release Level                                                            Number of approval levels released
User ID and Full Name                                            Who released
Release Date and Time                                           When it was released

Limitations
The release level assumes cumulative codes (X, XX, XXX). Check this against your own release strategy.
Reading change documents for many documents can be slow, so keep the selection narrow.
Add authorization checks before production use.
A toolbar “Back” button would be clearer than the SOURCE hotspot.


Conclusion
Out of the box, SAP doesn't give us a standard report that shows who approved a PO, when they did it, or how that PO links back to its parent PR, LTA, and Sales Order. This custom report bridges that gap perfectly.
By pulling data directly from the change document tables, the report lays out the exact approver, date, time, and release level for every document. The drill-down feature allows auditors to follow the entire chain—from PO to PR to LTA to SO—right inside a single ALV grid. Best of all, the history-stack design means you can easily navigate backward, one level at a time. It’s a highly reusable pattern you can drop into any ALV report that needs smooth drill-down navigation.
Feel free to take this template and customize it further by adding authorization checks, an Excel export feature, or even more document types. I hope this helps you build better, more auditor-friendly reports.
If you have any questions, suggestions, or a different way of handling this in your own projects, let me know in the comments below!


Thanks For Reading, Best Wishes
#ABAP Development

entry.title: Re: Inbound Delivery Not Created Automatically for Stock...
entry.content:
Recommended troubleshooting steps

1. Check the PO item confirmation control

Open ME23N and select the relevant PO item.

  • Go to Item Details → Confirmations.

  • Check whether a confirmation control key is maintained.

  • Confirm that it includes the Inbound Delivery / Shipping Notification confirmation category (LA).

  • Review whether an existing confirmation already covers the ordered quantity.

SAP requires the appropriate confirmation control for inbound delivery creation.

 

2. Check the PO quantity and existing confirmations

In ME23N, review the PO item and its PO history. If you have access to table display, check EKES for existing confirmations for that PO item.

Look for:

  • PO ordered quantity.

  • Existing inbound delivery or shipping notification quantities.

  • Goods receipts already posted.

  • Deleted or completed delivery indicators.

  • Any existing confirmation that has consumed the available notification quantity.

SAP documents ME160 as a possible result of exceeding the remaining notification quantity or the applicable delivery tolerance.

 

 

3. Investigate why this happens only with older POs

entry.title: Secure Your Cloud Integration iFlows with OAuth 2.0 Using SAP API Management
entry.content:
Imagine a third party needs to call your integration flow. You don't want to hand over your Cloud Integration service key. You'd rather give them a separate key and secret that you can control, revoke, and track per product.

SAP API Management in Integration Suite lets you do exactly that. In this blog, you'll build:

  1. A "Generate Token" proxy, which issues OAuth access tokens
  2. An iFlow proxy, which verifies those tokens before letting requests through
  3. A product and subscription, which provide the key and secret for consumers
  4. A test in Postman or Bruno, to see it all work

The Big Picture

Client (Postman/3rd party)
             │ 1. Key + Secret
            ▼
[Generate Token Proxy] ──► Access Token
           │
           │ 2. Call with Bearer Token
          ▼
[iFlow Proxy] ── Verify Token ──► Cloud Integration iFlow

 
Prerequisites

Before you start, make sure you have:

  • Access to SAP Integration Suite with the API Management capability enabled
  • A deployed iFlow that you want to expose
  • The service key of your Process Integration Runtime instance (plan: integration-flow). You'll need the client ID, client secret, and token URL.
  • Postman or Bruno for testing

Part 1: Create the "Generate Token" Proxy

This proxy is the endpoint your consumers will call to get an OAuth token.

Step 1: Create an API Provider 
  1. Open Integration Suite.
  2. Go to Configure → APIs → API Providers.
  3. Click Create.

     

  4. Enter a Name for your API Provider.


    Configure the connection

    Switch to the Connection tab and fill in the following:


    Field
    Value
    TypeCloud Integration
    HostThe host from the url in your service key (see tip below)
    Port443
    AuthenticationOAuth2ClientCredentials
    Client IDclientid from the service key
    Client Secretclientsecret from the service key
    Token URLtokenurl from the service key

    Tip:     Use the service key of your Process Integration Runtime instance with plan api. For the host, copy only the domain from the url field, without https:// and without any path.
    Then click Save.

 

Test the connection

Click Test Connection. If everything is set up correctly, you'll see a success message like this:

 

Your API Provider is ready! We'll use it later to expose your iFlow through an API proxy.

Step 2: Create the API Proxy

  1. Under Configure → APIs, click Create to create a new API proxy.
  2. Select URL as the source.
  3. Enter any placeholder URL. It must start with https:// and end with .com (for example, https://example.com).
  4. Give your proxy a Name and a Title.
  5. Enter a Base Path of your choice. It becomes part of your proxy endpoint URL.
  6. Click Create.
    Tip: The URL is only a placeholder. This proxy never calls it, because the OAuth policy that we add next responds to the request itself.

🎉Your proxy exists. Now we make it generate tokens.

Step 3: Add the OAuth v2.0 policy (GenerateAccessToken)
  1. Open your proxy and click Policies.

     

  2. Go to Proxy Endpoint → PreFlow in the left panel.
  3. On the right, find the OAuth v2.0 SET policy and click the + icon.
  4. Give the policy a name and click Add.
  5. Paste this XML:

<OAuthV2 async="false" continueOnError="false" enabled="true" xmlns="http://www.sap.com/apimgmt">
    <Operation>GenerateAccessToken</Operation>
    <GenerateResponse/>
    <SupportedGrantTypes>
        <GrantType>client_credentials</GrantType>
    </SupportedGrantTypes>
</OAuthV2>​

 


What does this policy do?
It generates and returns an OAuth access token for a client application using the client_credentials grant type. This grant type is the usual choice for system-to-system communication, where no end user logs in.
  1. Click Update → Save → Deploy.

Checkpoint: Copy the proxy endpoint URL. This is your Token URL, and you'll need it in the testing step.

Part 2: Create the Proxy for Your iFlow

Now we expose the actual iFlow and protect it.

Step 1: Before creating the iFlow proxy, you need the Cloud Integration API Provider that we created in Part 1 → Step 1. The proxy uses it to connect to your Cloud Integration tenant.
Step 2: Create the API Proxy from the Provider

This time, don't choose URL. Instead:

  1. Create a new API proxy and select Provider as the source.
  2. Choose the Cloud Integration provider you just created.
  3. Click Discover and select the iFlow you want to expose.
  4. Click Next.


Step 3: Configure authentication to the backend

On the next screen:

  • Authentication Type: OAuth2ClientCredentials
  • Client ID and Client Secret: from your Process Integration Runtime service key
  • Token URL: also from the service key

     

Don't mix these up!
The credentials here are the service key values (Plan - iflow), used by API Management to talk to Cloud Integration. Your consumers will later use a different key and secret, generated from the product subscription.

Step 4: Finalize the proxy details
  • Adjust the Base Path if you like. It appears in your endpoint URL.
  • Leave the other settings as they are.
  • Choose the Service Type that matches your iFlow's sender adapter (for example SOAP or REST).
  • Click Create.

     

🎉Your iFlow proxy is created.

Step 5: Add the OAuth v2.0 policy (VerifyAccessToken)
  1. Open Policies and add an OAuth v2.0 policy.
  2. Paste this XML:

<OAuthV2 async="false" continueOnError="true" enabled="true" xmlns="http://www.sap.com/apimgmt">
    <ExternalAuthorization>false</ExternalAuthorization>
    <Operation>VerifyAccessToken</Operation>
    <GenerateResponse enabled="true"/>
    <SupportedGrantTypes/>
    <Tokens/>
</OAuthV2>​

 


What does this policy do?
It verifies the access token sent by the client. If the token is valid, the request goes through. If not, an error response is returned. Place it on any protected API so that only authenticated clients get in.
  1. Click Update → Save → Deploy.

Checkpoint: You now have an endpoint URL for your iFlow proxy. Keep it handy.

Part 3: Bundle Everything into a Product

Consumers don't subscribe to individual proxies. They subscribe to products. So let's create one containing both proxies.

Step 1: Create the product
  1. Go to Engage → Products.
  2. Click Create.
  3. Enter a Name for the product.

Step 2: Add your proxies
  1. Open the APIs tab.
  2. Add both proxies:
    • ✔️The Generate Token proxy
    • ✔️The iFlow proxy

Why both?
Consumers need one to get the token and the other to use it. If either is missing from the product, the flow breaks.

Step 3: Publish

Click Publish to make the product available.

Part 4: Subscribe in the Developer Hub

Step 1: Open the Developer Hub

Step 2: Find your product and subscribe
  1. Search for your product and open it.

     

  2. From the Subscribe dropdown, select New subscription for application.

     

  3. Give the subscription a name and click Create.

     

Step 3: Grab your credentials 

After the subscription is created, you'll see a Key and a Secret.

  • They act as your Client ID and Client Secret for OAuth 2.0.
  • You can share them with third parties.
  • Every product subscription gets its own key and secret, so you can manage each consumer separately.

Part 5: Test It in Postman or Bruno 

Step 1: Set up the request
  1. Create a new request with the iFlow proxy endpoint URL.
  2. Under Auth, choose OAuth 2.0.
  3. Set Grant Type to Client Credentials.

Step 2: Fill in the token details

 

Field
Value
Access Token URLThe URL of your Generate Token proxy (Part 1)
Client IDKey from the Developer Hub
Client SecretSecret from the Developer Hub

Step 3: Generate the token and send the request
  1. Click Get / Generate Access Token.
  2. Use the token in your request.
  3. Send the request to your iFlow proxy endpoint.

🎉Success!

Quick Recap
  1. ✅Created a Generate Token proxy with the GenerateAccessToken policy
  2. ✅Created an iFlow proxy with the VerifyAccessToken policy
  3. ✅Bundled both into a product and published it
  4. ✅Subscribed in the Developer Hub to get a key and secret
  5. ✅Tested the flow in Postman or Bruno
Over to you!

Did this setup work for you? Are you using OAuth 2.0 for other scenarios, such as different grant types or custom scopes? Share your experience or questions in the comments below. I'd love to hear how you're securing your APIs.

If you found this helpful, give it a 👍 and follow me for more SAP Integration Suite content.

entry.title: How Komatsu Accelerated S/4HANA 2023 with Clean Core and SAP Joule for Developers
entry.content:
Implementing Clean Core Governance on S/4HANA 2023: Lessons from the Field

We work on the SAP team at Komatsu, one of the world's largest manufacturers of construction and mining equipment. Over the past year, we have been running an S/4HANA 2023 transformation program and set up a Clean Core governance model from scratch. This post shares the technical decisions, configuration steps, and practical lessons from that work, specifically the A-D object classification, ATC setup on S/4HANA 2023, Cloudification Repository usage, and how we remediated Level C and D findings.

Why Clean Core Matters for Upgrade Safety

Before our transformation, Komatsu's ECC landscape had accumulated hundreds of custom objects User Exits, BAdIs, Business Transaction Events (BTEs), VOFM Routines, and Web Dynpro screens. Each one is a potential blocker during an S/4HANA upgrade. SAP Clean Core is not a product; it is a strategy: keep the S/4HANA digital core as close to standard as possible and route business-specific extensions outside the core using loosely coupled patterns on SAP BTP.

The fundamental architectural shift this requires is moving computation from the ABAP application server down to SAP HANA. Classic SELECT * with joins and internal table processing needs to be replaced by CDS View entities, ABAP RAP business objects, and AMDP-based pushdown logic. This is not just a syntax change it requires developers to think differently about where logic runs.

The SAP Innovation Cycle: Six-Step Transformation Framework

A six-phase, AI-augmented approach that moves from initial exploration through to a fully upgrade-ready, AI-integrated digital core. The following phases reflect how we structured our own program this is not an official SAP methodology.

 

 

Here, the goal is not just to prepare the system for future innovations, but to make it truly AI-ready empowering us to harness the value of AI today while building a foundation for the breakthroughs of tomorrow.

The Four-Level Classification Framework (A-D)

The core of our governance model is a four-level extensibility classification aligned with SAP Note #3578329 and the Cloudification Repository Viewer. Every custom object is classified based on upgrade risk before any development begins.

  • SAP Clean Core Governance Framework

Table 1: Clean Core extensibility levels per SAP Note #3578329

Level

Name

Upgrade Risk

Examples

A

Gold Standard

Zero

Cloud-released APIs, Key User Extensibility, Developer Extensibility (ABAP Cloud), BTP Side-By-Side

B

Classic

Low

RAP BOs, CDS Views, CDS Table Functions, AMDP Methods, Cloud-Released BAdIs, Classes/Interfaces

C

Internal Objects

Medium

SAP Internal Objects, BDC, SAP Queries (SQ00/SQ01)

D

Not Recommended

High

Implicit/Explicit Enhancements, VOFM Pricing Routines, Web Dynpro ABAP

Every new requirement first goes through a Fit-to-Standard check. If standard SAP covers the requirement, no custom development is initiated. If a genuine gap exists, the requirement is routed through our governance decision tree. Level A on-stack options (Key User Extensibility, Developer Extensibility) are evaluated first; if not possible, Level B patterns (RAP, CDS, AMDP) are used. Level C and D objects require explicit approval and are added to an upgrade watch list for remediation in the next release cycle.

ATC Configuration for S/4HANA 2023 FPS03

One of the first practical challenges we encountered: the clean core ATC checks are not natively available in S/4HANA 2023. They are delivered out of the box only from S/4HANA 2025. For 2023 systems, you need to implement the following SAP Notes in order.

  • SAP Note 3565942:  Delivers the 'Usage of APIs' and 'Allowed Enhancement Technologies' ATC checks to S/4HANA 2023 systems
  • SAP Note 3627152: Note Analyzer files and bug fixes for the clean core checks; run the Note Analyzer after implementation to verify all recommended notes are current
  • SAP Note 3593439: Excludes key-user-generated objects from clean core ATC findings so they are not wrongly flagged as Level C

After implementing Note 3565942, open the check object SYCM_USAGE_OF_APIS in ADT for Eclipse and choose 'Import Parameters.' This step is easy to miss without it, the check does not have the API classification data it needs to run.

The prebuilt ABAP_CLEAN_CORE_DEVELOPMENT check variant is only available for ATC on SAP BTP or for S/4HANA 2025 FPS01 and above. On 2023, you build the variant manually: go to transaction ATC > Manage Check Variants > Global, copy ABAP_CLOUD_DEVELOPMENT_DEFAULT, and name it (we used ATC_CHECK_RWSMD). Then manually add the 'Usage of APIs' and 'Allowed Enhancement Technologies' checks under the Clean Core category, along with SYCM_ALLOWED_ENH_TECHNOLOGY. Keep the variant focused bundling in unrelated ATC checks causes problems because the RISE Methodology dashboard ignores them and the export can exceed the 100 MB import limit.

Since S/4HANA 2023 qualifies as '2023 and above,' you can run ATC locally via transaction ATC and export the results as a ZIP file (Scenario 1 — Local ATC Check). Import the file into Cloud ALM via: CALM Home > Services > SAP Readiness Check > Create New Analysis. Pre-requisite: the ALM_DEVELOPER role must be assigned to the user in Cloud ALM.

Using the Cloudification Repository to Resolve Level C and D Findings

The SAP Cloudification Repository Viewer is the practical tool for finding successors to deprecated or restricted APIs. When ATC flags an object, we use the repository to check whether a clean alternative exists before deciding how to handle it. The viewer is available at GitHub: sap.github.io/abap-atc-cr-cv-s4hc

Level D example BAPI replacement: We had a use of BAPI_CUSTOMER_GETDETAIL2 flagged as Level D. Checking the Cloudification Repository, the successor is the classic API CL_MDBPCVI_READER. We replaced the BAPI call with this class.

Not every Level D finding has a clean successor. We encountered a direct table update that was flagged Level D, but the code was deployed as part of SAP Note 0001790318. In cases like this, the governance process requires the developer to document that no alternative exists before the object receives an approval exception.

Level C example Table-to-CDS replacement: Several custom objects were flagged because developers used database tables directly instead of released CDS Views. The fix is straightforward once you know the mapping. The following table lists the replacements we applied based on the Cloudification Repository.

Table 2: Direct table references replaced with released CDS Views (source: Cloudification Repository Viewer, S/4HANA 2023 SP2)

Original Table

Released CDS View Replacement

AUFK (Maintenance Orders — AIFH)

I_MaintenanceOrder

MARA (Material)

I_producttp_2

CRMS4_SERV_H (Service Document)

I_SERVICEDOCUMENT

EQUI (Equipment)

I_Equipment

VBAK (Sales Document Header)

I_SalesDocument

VBAP (Sales Document Item)

I_SalesDocumentItem

Any object classified as Level C or D is registered on our upgrade watch list. This ensures technical debt is tracked and remediation is planned before the next S/4HANA version cycle, rather than discovered during the upgrade.

Code Pushdown: The Architectural Shift Developers Need to Internalize

Governance frameworks only work if developers understand the underlying architectural principle. In ECC, computation happened on the ABAP application server SELECT * queries pulled large datasets, and joins, loops, and aggregations ran in ABAP. In S/4HANA, the right model pushes logic down to SAP HANA using CDS Views and RAP. The application server becomes thin; HANA does the heavy lifting in-memory.

Table 3: ECC vs. S/4HANA computation model

Dimension

ECC Approach

S/4HANA Approach

Computation Layer

ABAP Application Server (joins, loops, aggregations)

SAP HANA in-memory DB via CDS Views and RAP

Data Transfer

SELECT * pulls millions of rows to app server

Only small, aggregated result set returned

Resource Consumption

High memory and CPU on application server

Thin logic heavy lifting delegated to database

UI Layer

SAP GUI / classic ABAP reports

SAP Fiori UI (RAP-based applications)

SAP Joule for Developers: Practical Experience

We integrated SAP Joule for Developers (J4D) SAP's AI co-pilot within the development environment to support clean core-compliant development. J4D is useful for several tasks: generating ABAP unit tests, producing RAP business object scaffolding, suggesting CDS-based refactoring for classic SELECT patterns, and explaining complex legacy ABAP code during knowledge transfer sessions.

Based on our internal observations on Level A and B extensibility objects new RAP-based developments where developers followed the clean core patterns we saw noticeably faster throughput compared to manual RICEFW development. We have not formally measured this against a controlled baseline, so we treat the improvement as a qualitative observation rather than a published metric.

J4D operates across two surfaces: SAP Build Code (pro-code, ABAP Cloud environment) for developer extensibility and RAP/wrapper object development, and SAP Build Apps (low-code) for key user extensibility and Fiori application generation.

 

Governance Decision Tree in Practice

Every new requirement goes through this routing logic before a single line of code is written:

 

Table 4: Clean Core governance decision routing

Decision Point

On-Stack Path

Side-By-Side BTP Path

Level A available?

Key User Extensibility, Developer Extensibility

Build Apps, Build Code, Process Automation, Build Work Zone

Level A not possible → Level B

RAP BO, CDS Views, CDS Table Functions, AMDP, Cloud-Released BAdIs

Wrapper pattern for classic APIs lacking a released successor

Legacy objects (Level C/D)

User Exit, Customer Exit, BAdI, BTE Classical Enhancement + Watch List

BDC, SAP Queries, Implicit/Explicit Enhancements, VOFM, Web Dynpro Exceptional Approval Required

Key Lessons for Other Teams

  • Set up the ATC variant before development starts, not after retroactive remediation is significantly more expensive
  • Implement SAP Notes 3565942, 3627152, and 3593439 before running any clean core checks on S/4HANA 2023; without them, the results are incomplete
  • Always import parameters for SYCM_USAGE_OF_APIS in ADT after implementing Note 3565942 it is a required step that the note documentation does not emphasize clearly
  • Use the Cloudification Repository Viewer to find successors before rejecting a Level C or D requirement as infeasible
  • Keep your ATC check variant lean only include clean core checks relevant to the RISE Methodology dashboard to avoid exceeding export limits
  • Register every Level C and D object in an upgrade watch list; without active tracking, technical debt becomes invisible

entry.title: Re: delete employee central users from LMS
entry.content:
Hi @user116 : 

Before we proceed further, there is an important point to mention i.e. you cannot simply delete an EC-Integrated User from Learning.

When SF Learning is integrated with Employee Central (via the SuccessFactors Platform), Learning does not own those user records because EC/Platform does.

If you delete a user directly in Learning while they are still active in EC, the next sync job (IPS or the standard Learning-Platform integration) will recreate the user in Learning. The deletion will not stick.

This is also documented as "The user account cannot be deleted until the User Source System is updated."  in the KBA 3614423

So the best approach here is to do the below which is a bit tricky because it works against the integration design. 

Step 1 — Inactivate the user in Learning first (do not delete the user yet)

  • Go to Learning Admin Center — Users, find the user, and set their status to Inactive.
  • A prompt will appear asking whether to cancel active registrations/waitlists — choose based on business need.
  • This hides the user from Learning workflows without removing transactional history.

Step 2 — Change the User Source System to "Learning"

  • This is the critical step that breaks the EC sync link for this user.
  • Navigate to System Administration — System Management Tools — Import Data.
  • Download the User template, populate it with the relevant user(s), and set the "userSourceSystem" field to "Learning". 
  • Re-import the file. This converts the user to a Learning-native record, meaning EC sync will no longer govern it.

Step 3 — Manually delete the user in Learning

  • Go to System Admin — Users, find the user, and use Delete.
  • At this stage deletion is possible because the user is no longer EC-governed.

NOTE: We would like to inform you that the deletion removes the user from transactional tables (PA tables). Learning history is preserved in audit/history tables (PH tables) but the user will not appear in standard reports.

This step should only be taken if the intention is full removal from Learning. Reference: Stages of User Data Removal in Learning

IPS Related Note: If the tenant uses IPS job to sync users, make sure that the IPS job filter is updated to exclude this user you wanted to delete. Otherwise IPS may recreate the user in Learning on the next run. You can refer to the KBA 3079849.


-Yashwanth.
